v: Paul, a servant[^1] of Christ Jesus, called to be an apostle, set apart for the good news of God,
Παῦλος δοῦλος Χριστοῦ Ἰησοῦ, κλητὸς ἀπόστολος, ἀφωρισμένος εἰς εὐαγγέλιον θεοῦ
which he promised beforehand through his prophets in the holy scriptures,
ὃ προεπηγγείλατο διὰ τῶν προφητῶν αὐτοῦ ἐν γραφαῖς ἁγίαις
concerning his Son, who was born a descendant of David according to the flesh[^2]
περὶ τοῦ υἱοῦ αὐτοῦ, τοῦ γενομένου ἐκ σπέρματος Δαυὶδ κατὰ σάρκα,
and was appointed[^3] Son of God in power according to the Spirit of holiness[^4] by the resurrection from the dead:[^5] Jesus Christ our Lord.
τοῦ ὁρισθέντος υἱοῦ θεοῦ ἐν δυνάμει κατὰ πνεῦμα ἁγιωσύνης ἐξ ἀναστάσεως νεκρῶν, Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ τοῦ κυρίου ἡμῶν,
Through him we received grace and apostleship to bring about the obedience of faith[^6] among all the Gentiles[^7] for the sake of his name,
διʼ οὗ ἐλάβομεν χάριν καὶ ἀποστολὴν εἰς ὑπακοὴν πίστεως ἐν πᾶσιν τοῖς ἔθνεσιν ὑπὲρ τοῦ ὀνόματος αὐτοῦ,
and you too are among them, called to belong to Jesus Christ.[^8]
ἐν οἷς ἐστε καὶ ὑμεῖς κλητοὶ Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ,
To all who are in Rome, loved by God and called to be God's holy people:[^9] Grace to you and peace from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.
πᾶσιν τοῖς οὖσιν ἐν Ῥώμῃ ἀγαπητοῖς θεοῦ, κλητοῖς ἁγίοις· χάρις ὑμῖν καὶ εἰρήνη ἀπὸ θεοῦ πατρὸς ἡμῶν καὶ κυρίου Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ.
First, I thank my God through Jesus Christ for all of you, because your faith is being proclaimed in the whole world.
Πρῶτον μὲν εὐχαριστῶ τῷ θεῷ μου διὰ Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ περὶ πάντων ὑμῶν, ὅτι ἡ πίστις ὑμῶν καταγγέλλεται ἐν ὅλῳ τῷ κόσμῳ.
For God, whom I serve with my spirit in the good news of his Son,[^10] is my witness how constantly I remember you
μάρτυς γάρ μού ἐστιν ὁ θεός, ᾧ λατρεύω ἐν τῷ πνεύματί μου ἐν τῷ εὐαγγελίῳ τοῦ υἱοῦ αὐτοῦ, ὡς ἀδιαλείπτως μνείαν ὑμῶν ποιοῦμαι
in my prayers at all times, asking that somehow, now at last, by the will of God I may succeed in coming to you.
πάντοτε ἐπὶ τῶν προσευχῶν μου, δεόμενος εἴ πως ἤδη ποτὲ εὐοδωθήσομαι ἐν τῷ θελήματι τοῦ θεοῦ ἐλθεῖν πρὸς ὑμᾶς.
For I long to see you, so that I may share some spiritual gift with you to strengthen you,
ἐπιποθῶ γὰρ ἰδεῖν ὑμᾶς, ἵνα τι μεταδῶ χάρισμα ὑμῖν πνευματικὸν εἰς τὸ στηριχθῆναι ὑμᾶς,
that is, so that we may be encouraged together while I am among you, each by the other's faith, both yours and mine.
τοῦτο δέ ἐστιν συμπαρακληθῆναι ἐν ὑμῖν διὰ τῆς ἐν ἀλλήλοις πίστεως ὑμῶν τε καὶ ἐμοῦ.

I do not want you to be unaware, brothers and sisters,[^11] that I have often planned to come to you (but have been prevented until now), so that I might have some fruit among you too, just as among the rest of the Gentiles.
οὐ θέλω δὲ ὑμᾶς ἀγνοεῖν, ἀδελφοί, ὅτι πολλάκις προεθέμην ἐλθεῖν πρὸς ὑμᾶς, καὶ ἐκωλύθην ἄχρι τοῦ δεῦρο, ἵνα τινὰ καρπὸν σχῶ καὶ ἐν ὑμῖν καθὼς καὶ ἐν τοῖς λοιποῖς ἔθνεσιν.
I am under obligation both to Greeks and to non-Greeks,[^12] both to the wise and to the foolish.
Ἕλλησίν τε καὶ βαρβάροις, σοφοῖς τε καὶ ἀνοήτοις ὀφειλέτης εἰμί·
So, for my part, I am eager to proclaim the good news to you also who are in Rome.
οὕτως τὸ κατʼ ἐμὲ πρόθυμον καὶ ὑμῖν τοῖς ἐν Ῥώμῃ εὐαγγελίσασθαι.
For I am not ashamed of the good news,[^13] because it is the power of God for salvation to everyone who believes, to the Jew first and also to the Greek.
Οὐ γὰρ ἐπαισχύνομαι τὸ εὐαγγέλιον, δύναμις γὰρ θεοῦ ἐστιν εἰς σωτηρίαν παντὶ τῷ πιστεύοντι, Ἰουδαίῳ τε πρῶτον καὶ Ἕλληνι·
For in it the righteousness of God[^14] is revealed from faith to faith,[^15] as it is written, "But the righteous will live by faith."[^16]
δικαιοσύνη γὰρ θεοῦ ἐν αὐτῷ ἀποκαλύπτεται ἐκ πίστεως εἰς πίστιν, καθὼς γέγραπται· Ὁ δὲ δίκαιος ἐκ πίστεως ζήσεται.
For the wrath of God is being revealed from heaven against all the ungodliness and unrighteousness of people who by their unrighteousness suppress the truth,
Ἀποκαλύπτεται γὰρ ὀργὴ θεοῦ ἀπʼ οὐρανοῦ ἐπὶ πᾶσαν ἀσέβειαν καὶ ἀδικίαν ἀνθρώπων τῶν τὴν ἀλήθειαν ἐν ἀδικίᾳ κατεχόντων,
because what can be known about God is plain to them,[^17] for God has made it plain to them.
διότι τὸ γνωστὸν τοῦ θεοῦ φανερόν ἐστιν ἐν αὐτοῖς, ὁ θεὸς γὰρ αὐτοῖς ἐφανέρωσεν.

For since the creation of the world his invisible qualities, his eternal power and divine nature, have been clearly seen, being understood through the things he has made, so that they are without excuse,
τὰ γὰρ ἀόρατα αὐτοῦ ἀπὸ κτίσεως κόσμου τοῖς ποιήμασιν νοούμενα καθορᾶται, ἥ τε ἀΐδιος αὐτοῦ δύναμις καὶ θειότης, εἰς τὸ εἶναι αὐτοὺς ἀναπολογήτους,
because, although they knew God, they did not glorify him as God or give thanks to him. Instead, they became futile in their thinking, and their senseless hearts were darkened.
διότι γνόντες τὸν θεὸν οὐχ ὡς θεὸν ἐδόξασαν ἢ ηὐχαρίστησαν, ἀλλὰ ἐματαιώθησαν ἐν τοῖς διαλογισμοῖς αὐτῶν καὶ ἐσκοτίσθη ἡ ἀσύνετος αὐτῶν καρδία·
Claiming to be wise, they became fools,
φάσκοντες εἶναι σοφοὶ ἐμωράνθησαν,
and they exchanged the glory of the immortal God for images made to look like a mortal human being, and birds, and four-footed animals, and reptiles.[^18]
καὶ ἤλλαξαν τὴν δόξαν τοῦ ἀφθάρτου θεοῦ ἐν ὁμοιώματι εἰκόνος φθαρτοῦ ἀνθρώπου καὶ πετεινῶν καὶ τετραπόδων καὶ ἑρπετῶν.
Therefore God handed them over[^19] in the desires of their hearts to impurity, so that they dishonored their bodies among themselves.
Διὸ παρέδωκεν αὐτοὺς ὁ θεὸς ἐν ταῖς ἐπιθυμίαις τῶν καρδιῶν αὐτῶν εἰς ἀκαθαρσίαν τοῦ ἀτιμάζεσθαι τὰ σώματα αὐτῶν ἐν αὐτοῖς,
They exchanged the truth of God for the lie, and worshiped and served the creation rather than the Creator, who is blessed forever. Amen.
οἵτινες μετήλλαξαν τὴν ἀλήθειαν τοῦ θεοῦ ἐν τῷ ψεύδει, καὶ ἐσεβάσθησαν καὶ ἐλάτρευσαν τῇ κτίσει παρὰ τὸν κτίσαντα, ὅς ἐστιν εὐλογητὸς εἰς τοὺς αἰῶνας· ἀμήν.
For this reason God handed them over to dishonorable passions. For their women exchanged natural relations[^20] for those that are against nature,
Διὰ τοῦτο παρέδωκεν αὐτοὺς ὁ θεὸς εἰς πάθη ἀτιμίας· αἵ τε γὰρ θήλειαι αὐτῶν μετήλλαξαν τὴν φυσικὴν χρῆσιν εἰς τὴν παρὰ φύσιν,

and in the same way the men also gave up natural relations with women and were inflamed with their desire for one another, men committing shameless acts with men and receiving in themselves the penalty their error deserved.

ὁμοίως τε καὶ οἱ ἄρσενες ἀφέντες τὴν φυσικὴν χρῆσιν τῆς θηλείας ἐξεκαύθησαν ἐν τῇ ὀρέξει αὐτῶν εἰς ἀλλήλους, ἄρσενες ἐν ἄρσεσιν τὴν ἀσχημοσύνην κατεργαζόμενοι καὶ τὴν ἀντιμισθίαν ἣν ἔδει τῆς πλάνης αὐτῶν ἐν ἑαυτοῖς ἀπολαμβάνοντες.
And since they did not see fit to acknowledge God, God handed them over to an unfit mind,[^21] to do what ought not to be done.
Καὶ καθὼς οὐκ ἐδοκίμασαν τὸν θεὸν ἔχειν ἐν ἐπιγνώσει, παρέδωκεν αὐτοὺς ὁ θεὸς εἰς ἀδόκιμον νοῦν, ποιεῖν τὰ μὴ καθήκοντα,
They are filled with every kind of unrighteousness,[^22] wickedness, greed and malice. They are full of envy, murder, strife, deceit and spite. They are gossips,
πεπληρωμένους πάσῃ ἀδικίᾳ πονηρίᾳ πλεονεξίᾳ κακίᾳ, μεστοὺς φθόνου φόνου ἔριδος δόλου κακοηθείας, ψιθυριστάς,
slanderers, haters of God,[^23] insolent, arrogant, boastful, inventors of evil, disobedient to parents,
καταλάλους, θεοστυγεῖς, ὑβριστάς, ὑπερηφάνους, ἀλαζόνας, ἐφευρετὰς κακῶν, γονεῦσιν ἀπειθεῖς,
senseless, faithless, heartless,[^24] merciless.
ἀσυνέτους, ἀσυνθέτους, ἀστόργους, ἀνελεήμονας·
Although they know God's righteous decree, that those who practice such things deserve death, they not only do them but also approve of those who practice them.
οἵτινες τὸ δικαίωμα τοῦ θεοῦ ἐπιγνόντες, ὅτι οἱ τὰ τοιαῦτα πράσσοντες ἄξιοι θανάτου εἰσίν, οὐ μόνον αὐτὰ ποιοῦσιν ἀλλὰ καὶ συνευδοκοῦσιν τοῖς πράσσουσιν.

n.2: That is, by human descent. Literally "who came from the seed of David according to the flesh". Here *flesh* (Greek *sarx*) means human nature, not the flesh in Paul's moral sense (see 7:5). It stands in contrast to "according to the Spirit of holiness" in verse 4.
n.3: Or "declared". Greek *horizo*, "mark out, appoint". *In power* may go with "Son of God" ("the Son of God in power") or with "appointed" ("powerfully appointed").
n.4: That is, the Holy Spirit. Or "according to the spirit of holiness", his own holy nature.
n.5: Literally "from the resurrection of the dead". *From* may mean "by" or "since".
n.6: Literally "for obedience of faith". Or "the obedience that comes from faith", or "the obedience that is faith".
n.7: Or "nations". Greek *ethne* means both; also in verse 13.
n.8: Literally "called of Jesus Christ". Or "called by Jesus Christ".
n.9: Literally "called holy ones"; traditionally "called to be saints".
n.10: That is, in proclaiming the good news of his Son.
n.11: Greek *adelphoi*, "brothers", used of the believers, men and women alike.
n.12: Greek *barbaroi*, people who did not speak Greek.
n.13: Many manuscripts read "the good news of Christ".
n.14: Or "the righteousness that comes from God". Greek *dikaiosyne*, "righteousness, justice". The phrase can mean God's own righteousness, his justice and faithfulness, or the right standing he gives.
n.15: Literally "from faith into faith". Or "by faith from first to last", or "from God's faithfulness to human faith". Greek *pistis* means both "faith" and "faithfulness".
n.16: Habakkuk 2:4. Or "The one who is righteous by faith will live." The Hebrew has "by his faithfulness", and the Septuagint "by my faithfulness", that is, God's; Paul has neither "his" nor "my". Also quoted in Galatians 3:11.
n.18: Literally "for the likeness of an image of a mortal human being and of birds and of four-footed animals and of reptiles". Compare Psalm 106:20; Deuteronomy 4:16–18.
n.19: Many manuscripts read "Therefore God also handed them over".
n.20: Literally "the natural use", here of sexual relations; also in verse 27.
n.21: *Did not see fit* and *unfit* translate related Greek words: *dokimazo*, "test, approve", and *adokimos*, "failing the test, worthless".

v: Therefore you have no excuse, whoever you are,[^1] when you pass judgment. For in judging another, you condemn yourself, because you, the judge, do the same things.
Διὸ ἀναπολόγητος εἶ, ὦ ἄνθρωπε πᾶς ὁ κρίνων· ἐν ᾧ γὰρ κρίνεις τὸν ἕτερον, σεαυτὸν κατακρίνεις, τὰ γὰρ αὐτὰ πράσσεις ὁ κρίνων·
We know that God's judgment on those who do such things is in accordance with the truth.
οἴδαμεν δὲ ὅτι τὸ κρίμα τοῦ θεοῦ ἐστιν κατὰ ἀλήθειαν ἐπὶ τοὺς τὰ τοιαῦτα πράσσοντας.
Do you suppose, you who judge those who do such things and yet do them yourself, that you will escape the judgment of God?
λογίζῃ δὲ τοῦτο, ὦ ἄνθρωπε ὁ κρίνων τοὺς τὰ τοιαῦτα πράσσοντας καὶ ποιῶν αὐτά, ὅτι σὺ ἐκφεύξῃ τὸ κρίμα τοῦ θεοῦ;
Or do you despise the riches of his kindness and forbearance and patience, not knowing that God's kindness is leading you to repentance?
ἢ τοῦ πλούτου τῆς χρηστότητος αὐτοῦ καὶ τῆς ἀνοχῆς καὶ τῆς μακροθυμίας καταφρονεῖς, ἀγνοῶν ὅτι τὸ χρηστὸν τοῦ θεοῦ εἰς μετάνοιάν σε ἄγει;
But because of your hardness and your unrepentant heart, you are storing up wrath for yourself on the day of wrath, when the righteous judgment of God is revealed.[^2]
κατὰ δὲ τὴν σκληρότητά σου καὶ ἀμετανόητον καρδίαν θησαυρίζεις σεαυτῷ ὀργὴν ἐν ἡμέρᾳ ὀργῆς καὶ ἀποκαλύψεως δικαιοκρισίας τοῦ θεοῦ,
He will repay each person according to what he has done:[^3]
ὃς ἀποδώσει ἑκάστῳ κατὰ τὰ ἔργα αὐτοῦ·
to those who by perseverance in doing good seek glory and honor and immortality, eternal life;
τοῖς μὲν καθʼ ὑπομονὴν ἔργου ἀγαθοῦ δόξαν καὶ τιμὴν καὶ ἀφθαρσίαν ζητοῦσιν ζωὴν αἰώνιον·
but for those who are self-seeking[^4] and disobey the truth but obey unrighteousness, wrath and fury.
τοῖς δὲ ἐξ ἐριθείας καὶ ἀπειθοῦσι τῇ ἀληθείᾳ πειθομένοις δὲ τῇ ἀδικίᾳ ὀργὴ καὶ θυμός,
There will be trouble and distress for every human being[^5] who does evil, the Jew first and also the Greek,
θλῖψις καὶ στενοχωρία, ἐπὶ πᾶσαν ψυχὴν ἀνθρώπου τοῦ κατεργαζομένου τὸ κακόν, Ἰουδαίου τε πρῶτον καὶ Ἕλληνος·
but glory and honor and peace for everyone who does good, the Jew first and also the Greek.
δόξα δὲ καὶ τιμὴ καὶ εἰρήνη παντὶ τῷ ἐργαζομένῳ τὸ ἀγαθόν, Ἰουδαίῳ τε πρῶτον καὶ Ἕλληνι·
For God shows no partiality.[^6]
οὐ γάρ ἐστιν προσωπολημψία παρὰ τῷ θεῷ.
For all who have sinned without the Law will also perish without the Law, and all who have sinned under the Law[^7] will be judged by the Law.
Ὅσοι γὰρ ἀνόμως ἥμαρτον, ἀνόμως καὶ ἀπολοῦνται· καὶ ὅσοι ἐν νόμῳ ἥμαρτον, διὰ νόμου κριθήσονται·
For it is not the hearers of the Law who are righteous before God, but the doers of the Law who will be declared righteous.[^8]
οὐ γὰρ οἱ ἀκροαταὶ νόμου δίκαιοι παρὰ τῷ θεῷ, ἀλλʼ οἱ ποιηταὶ νόμου δικαιωθήσονται.
For when Gentiles, who do not have the Law, do by nature what the Law requires,[^9] they are a law to themselves, even though they do not have the Law.
ὅταν γὰρ ἔθνη τὰ μὴ νόμον ἔχοντα φύσει τὰ τοῦ νόμου ποιῶσιν, οὗτοι νόμον μὴ ἔχοντες ἑαυτοῖς εἰσιν νόμος·
They show that the work of the Law[^10] is written on their hearts, while their conscience also bears witness, and their thoughts in turn accuse or even defend them,
οἵτινες ἐνδείκνυνται τὸ ἔργον τοῦ νόμου γραπτὸν ἐν ταῖς καρδίαις αὐτῶν, συμμαρτυρούσης αὐτῶν τῆς συνειδήσεως καὶ μεταξὺ ἀλλήλων τῶν λογισμῶν κατηγορούντων ἢ καὶ ἀπολογουμένων,
on the day when God judges the secrets of human beings according to my good news, through Christ Jesus.[^11]
ἐν ἡμέρᾳ ὅτε κρίνει ὁ θεὸς τὰ κρυπτὰ τῶν ἀνθρώπων κατὰ τὸ εὐαγγέλιόν μου διὰ Χριστοῦ Ἰησοῦ.
But if you call yourself a Jew,[^12] and rely on the Law, and boast in God,
Εἰ δὲ σὺ Ἰουδαῖος ἐπονομάζῃ καὶ ἐπαναπαύῃ νόμῳ καὶ καυχᾶσαι ἐν θεῷ
and know his will, and approve what is excellent[^13] because you are instructed from the Law,
καὶ γινώσκεις τὸ θέλημα καὶ δοκιμάζεις τὰ διαφέροντα κατηχούμενος ἐκ τοῦ νόμου,
and are confident that you are a guide to the blind, a light to those in darkness,
πέποιθάς τε σεαυτὸν ὁδηγὸν εἶναι τυφλῶν, φῶς τῶν ἐν σκότει,
an instructor of the foolish, a teacher of children, because you have in the Law the embodiment of knowledge and truth —
παιδευτὴν ἀφρόνων, διδάσκαλον νηπίων, ἔχοντα τὴν μόρφωσιν τῆς γνώσεως καὶ τῆς ἀληθείας ἐν τῷ νόμῳ—
you, then, who teach another, do you not teach yourself? You who preach that one must not steal, do you steal?
ὁ οὖν διδάσκων ἕτερον σεαυτὸν οὐ διδάσκεις; ὁ κηρύσσων μὴ κλέπτειν κλέπτεις;
You who say that one must not commit adultery, do you commit adultery? You who detest idols, do you rob temples?
ὁ λέγων μὴ μοιχεύειν μοιχεύεις; ὁ βδελυσσόμενος τὰ εἴδωλα ἱεροσυλεῖς;
You who boast in the Law, do you dishonor God by breaking the Law?
ὃς ἐν νόμῳ καυχᾶσαι, διὰ τῆς παραβάσεως τοῦ νόμου τὸν θεὸν ἀτιμάζεις;
For "the name of God is despised among the Gentiles because of you," as it is written.[^14]
τὸ γὰρ ὄνομα τοῦ θεοῦ διʼ ὑμᾶς βλασφημεῖται ἐν τοῖς ἔθνεσιν, καθὼς γέγραπται.
For circumcision is of value if you practice the Law; but if you break the Law, your circumcision has become uncircumcision.
Περιτομὴ μὲν γὰρ ὠφελεῖ ἐὰν νόμον πράσσῃς· ἐὰν δὲ παραβάτης νόμου ᾖς, ἡ περιτομή σου ἀκροβυστία γέγονεν.
So if an uncircumcised man keeps the requirements of the Law, will not his uncircumcision be counted as circumcision?
ἐὰν οὖν ἡ ἀκροβυστία τὰ δικαιώματα τοῦ νόμου φυλάσσῃ, οὐχ ἡ ἀκροβυστία αὐτοῦ εἰς περιτομὴν λογισθήσεται;
And the one who is physically uncircumcised but fulfills the Law will judge you, who, with the written code and circumcision, break the Law.[^15]
καὶ κρινεῖ ἡ ἐκ φύσεως ἀκροβυστία τὸν νόμον τελοῦσα σὲ τὸν διὰ γράμματος καὶ περιτομῆς παραβάτην νόμου.
For a person is not a Jew who is one outwardly, nor is circumcision what is outward, in the flesh.[^16]
οὐ γὰρ ὁ ἐν τῷ φανερῷ Ἰουδαῖός ἐστιν, οὐδὲ ἡ ἐν τῷ φανερῷ ἐν σαρκὶ περιτομή·
No, a person is a Jew who is one inwardly, and circumcision is circumcision of the heart, by the Spirit, not by the written code.[^17] That person's praise is not from people but from God.[^18]
ἀλλʼ ὁ ἐν τῷ κρυπτῷ Ἰουδαῖος, καὶ περιτομὴ καρδίας ἐν πνεύματι οὐ γράμματι, οὗ ὁ ἔπαινος οὐκ ἐξ ἀνθρώπων ἀλλʼ ἐκ τοῦ θεοῦ.

n.1: Literally "O man, everyone who judges". *O man* (Greek *o anthrope*) addresses an imagined listener, as in a debate; also in verse 3.
n.2: Many manuscripts read "the day of wrath and of revelation and of God's righteous judgment".
n.3: Psalm 62:13 (62:12 in most English Bibles); Proverbs 24:12. Literally "according to his works".
n.5: Literally "every soul of a human being".
n.6: Literally "there is no receiving of face with God", that is, no favoritism.
n.7: Literally "in the Law", that is, having the Law.
n.9: Or "For when Gentiles, who by nature do not have the Law, do what the Law requires". *By nature* may go with either part of the sentence.
n.10: That is, what the Law requires. Compare "the works of the Law" in 3:20, and Jeremiah 31:33.
n.11: Verse 16 may continue the thought of verses 12–13, with verses 14–15 as an aside.
n.12: Many manuscripts read "Look, you call yourself a Jew".
n.13: Or "discern what matters". Literally "test the things that differ".
n.14: Isaiah 52:5, as in the Septuagint, which reads "Because of you my name is despised among the nations". The Hebrew has "all day long my name is continually despised". Compare Ezekiel 36:20–23. *Despised*: Greek *blasphemeo*, "slander, revile, blaspheme".
n.15: Literally "who through letter and circumcision are a transgressor of the Law". *Letter* (Greek *gramma*) means the Law as written; also in verse 29.
n.16: That is, physical. Greek *sarx*, "flesh", here the body.
n.17: Or "in spirit, not in letter". Compare Deuteronomy 10:16; 30:6; Jeremiah 4:4.
n.18: There is a play on words. The name Judah, from which "Jew" comes, is explained in Genesis 29:35 by the Hebrew for "I will praise".

v: Then what advantage does the Jew have? Or what is the value of circumcision?
Τί οὖν τὸ περισσὸν τοῦ Ἰουδαίου, ἢ τίς ἡ ὠφέλεια τῆς περιτομῆς;
Much, in every way. For first of all, they were entrusted with the words[^1] of God.
πολὺ κατὰ πάντα τρόπον. πρῶτον μὲν γὰρ ὅτι ἐπιστεύθησαν τὰ λόγια τοῦ θεοῦ.
What then? If some were unfaithful, will their unfaithfulness nullify the faithfulness of God?[^2]
τί γάρ; εἰ ἠπίστησάν τινες, μὴ ἡ ἀπιστία αὐτῶν τὴν πίστιν τοῦ θεοῦ καταργήσει;
By no means![^3] Let God be true, and every human being a liar,[^4] as it is written: "So that you may be proved right[^5] in your words, and prevail when you are judged."[^6]
μὴ γένοιτο· γινέσθω δὲ ὁ θεὸς ἀληθής, πᾶς δὲ ἄνθρωπος ψεύστης, καθὼς γέγραπται· Ὅπως ἂν δικαιωθῇς ἐν τοῖς λόγοις σου καὶ νικήσεις ἐν τῷ κρίνεσθαί σε.
But if our unrighteousness shows God's righteousness, what shall we say? That God is unrighteous to inflict wrath? (I am speaking in a human way.)
εἰ δὲ ἡ ἀδικία ἡμῶν θεοῦ δικαιοσύνην συνίστησιν, τί ἐροῦμεν; μὴ ἄδικος ὁ θεὸς ὁ ἐπιφέρων τὴν ὀργήν; κατὰ ἄνθρωπον λέγω.
By no means! For then how could God judge the world?
μὴ γένοιτο· ἐπεὶ πῶς κρινεῖ ὁ θεὸς τὸν κόσμον;
But[^7] if through my falsehood God's truthfulness overflows to his glory, why am I still being judged as a sinner?
εἰ δὲ ἡ ἀλήθεια τοῦ θεοῦ ἐν τῷ ἐμῷ ψεύσματι ἐπερίσσευσεν εἰς τὴν δόξαν αὐτοῦ, τί ἔτι κἀγὼ ὡς ἁμαρτωλὸς κρίνομαι,
And why not say, as we are slanderously accused of saying, and as some claim that we say, "Let us do evil so that good may come"? Their condemnation is just.
καὶ μὴ καθὼς βλασφημούμεθα καὶ καθώς φασίν τινες ἡμᾶς λέγειν ὅτι Ποιήσωμεν τὰ κακὰ ἵνα ἔλθῃ τὰ ἀγαθά; ὧν τὸ κρίμα ἔνδικόν ἐστιν.
What then? Are we better off?[^8] Not at all. For we have already charged that all, both Jews and Greeks, are under the power of sin,[^9]
Τί οὖν; προεχόμεθα; οὐ πάντως, προῃτιασάμεθα γὰρ Ἰουδαίους τε καὶ Ἕλληνας πάντας ὑφʼ ἁμαρτίαν εἶναι,
as it is written: "There is no one righteous, not even one.
καθὼς γέγραπται ὅτι Οὐκ ἔστιν δίκαιος οὐδὲ εἷς,
There is no one who understands; there is no one who seeks God.
οὐκ ἔστιν ὁ συνίων, οὐκ ἔστιν ὁ ἐκζητῶν τὸν θεόν·
They have all turned aside; together they have become worthless. There is no one who does good, not even one.[^10]
πάντες ἐξέκλιναν, ἅμα ἠχρεώθησαν· οὐκ ἔστιν ποιῶν χρηστότητα, οὐκ ἔστιν ἕως ἑνός.
Their throat is an open grave; they deceive with their tongues.[^11] The venom of vipers is under their lips.[^12]
τάφος ἀνεῳγμένος ὁ λάρυγξ αὐτῶν, ταῖς γλώσσαις αὐτῶν ἐδολιοῦσαν, ἰὸς ἀσπίδων ὑπὸ τὰ χείλη αὐτῶν,
Their mouth is full of curses and bitterness.[^13]
ὧν τὸ στόμα ἀρᾶς καὶ πικρίας γέμει·
Their feet are swift to shed blood;
ὀξεῖς οἱ πόδες αὐτῶν ἐκχέαι αἷμα,
ruin and misery are in their paths,
σύντριμμα καὶ ταλαιπωρία ἐν ταῖς ὁδοῖς αὐτῶν,
and the way of peace they have not known.[^14]
καὶ ὁδὸν εἰρήνης οὐκ ἔγνωσαν.
There is no fear of God before their eyes."[^15]
οὐκ ἔστιν φόβος θεοῦ ἀπέναντι τῶν ὀφθαλμῶν αὐτῶν.
Now we know that whatever the Law says, it speaks to those who are under the Law,[^16] so that every mouth may be silenced and the whole world may be held accountable to God.
Οἴδαμεν δὲ ὅτι ὅσα ὁ νόμος λέγει τοῖς ἐν τῷ νόμῳ λαλεῖ, ἵνα πᾶν στόμα φραγῇ καὶ ὑπόδικος γένηται πᾶς ὁ κόσμος τῷ θεῷ·
For by works of the Law[^17] no human being[^18] will be declared righteous in his sight, for through the Law comes the knowledge of sin.
διότι ἐξ ἔργων νόμου οὐ δικαιωθήσεται πᾶσα σὰρξ ἐνώπιον αὐτοῦ, διὰ γὰρ νόμου ἐπίγνωσις ἁμαρτίας.
But now, apart from the Law, the righteousness of God has been made known, attested by the Law and the Prophets:
Νυνὶ δὲ χωρὶς νόμου δικαιοσύνη θεοῦ πεφανέρωται, μαρτυρουμένη ὑπὸ τοῦ νόμου καὶ τῶν προφητῶν,
the righteousness of God through faith in Jesus Christ[^19] for all who believe.[^20] For there is no distinction,
δικαιοσύνη δὲ θεοῦ διὰ πίστεως Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ, εἰς πάντας τοὺς πιστεύοντας, οὐ γάρ ἐστιν διαστολή.
for all have sinned and fall short of the glory of God,
πάντες γὰρ ἥμαρτον καὶ ὑστεροῦνται τῆς δόξης τοῦ θεοῦ,
and they are declared righteous freely by his grace through the redemption that is in Christ Jesus.
δικαιούμενοι δωρεὰν τῇ αὐτοῦ χάριτι διὰ τῆς ἀπολυτρώσεως τῆς ἐν Χριστῷ Ἰησοῦ·
God put him forward as a place of atonement[^21] through faith, by his blood,[^22] to demonstrate his righteousness, because he had passed over the sins committed beforehand[^23]
ὃν προέθετο ὁ θεὸς ἱλαστήριον διὰ πίστεως ἐν τῷ αὐτοῦ αἵματι εἰς ἔνδειξιν τῆς δικαιοσύνης αὐτοῦ διὰ τὴν πάρεσιν τῶν προγεγονότων ἁμαρτημάτων
in his forbearance. It was to demonstrate his righteousness at the present time, so that he would be righteous and would declare righteous the person who has faith in Jesus.[^24]
ἐν τῇ ἀνοχῇ τοῦ θεοῦ, πρὸς τὴν ἔνδειξιν τῆς δικαιοσύνης αὐτοῦ ἐν τῷ νῦν καιρῷ, εἰς τὸ εἶναι αὐτὸν δίκαιον καὶ δικαιοῦντα τὸν ἐκ πίστεως Ἰησοῦ.
Where, then, is boasting? It is excluded. By what kind of law?[^25] By the law of works? No, but by the law of faith.
Ποῦ οὖν ἡ καύχησις; ἐξεκλείσθη. διὰ ποίου νόμου; τῶν ἔργων; οὐχί, ἀλλὰ διὰ νόμου πίστεως.
For[^26] we hold that a person is declared righteous by faith apart from works of the Law.
λογιζόμεθα γὰρ δικαιοῦσθαι πίστει ἄνθρωπον χωρὶς ἔργων νόμου.
Or is God the God of Jews only? Is he not the God of Gentiles also? Yes, of Gentiles also,
ἢ Ἰουδαίων ὁ θεὸς μόνον; οὐχὶ καὶ ἐθνῶν; ναὶ καὶ ἐθνῶν,
since God is one,[^27] and he will declare righteous the circumcised by faith and the uncircumcised through faith.
εἴπερ εἷς ὁ θεός, ὃς δικαιώσει περιτομὴν ἐκ πίστεως καὶ ἀκροβυστίαν διὰ τῆς πίστεως.
Do we then nullify the Law through faith? By no means! On the contrary, we uphold the Law.
νόμον οὖν καταργοῦμεν διὰ τῆς πίστεως; μὴ γένοιτο, ἀλλὰ νόμον ἱστάνομεν.

v: What then shall we say that Abraham, our forefather according to the flesh,[^1] has found?[^2]
Τί οὖν ἐροῦμεν εὑρηκέναι Ἀβραὰμ τὸν προπάτορα ἡμῶν κατὰ σάρκα;
For if Abraham was declared righteous[^3] by works, he has something to boast about, but not before God.
εἰ γὰρ Ἀβραὰμ ἐξ ἔργων ἐδικαιώθη, ἔχει καύχημα· ἀλλʼ οὐ πρὸς θεόν,
For what does the scripture say? "Abraham believed God, and it was credited to him as righteousness."[^4]
τί γὰρ ἡ γραφὴ λέγει; Ἐπίστευσεν δὲ Ἀβραὰμ τῷ θεῷ καὶ ἐλογίσθη αὐτῷ εἰς δικαιοσύνην.
Now to the one who works, the wages are not credited as a gift[^5] but as what is owed.
τῷ δὲ ἐργαζομένῳ ὁ μισθὸς οὐ λογίζεται κατὰ χάριν ἀλλὰ κατὰ ὀφείλημα·
But to the one who does not work but believes in him who declares the ungodly righteous, his faith is credited as righteousness,
τῷ δὲ μὴ ἐργαζομένῳ, πιστεύοντι δὲ ἐπὶ τὸν δικαιοῦντα τὸν ἀσεβῆ, λογίζεται ἡ πίστις αὐτοῦ εἰς δικαιοσύνην,
just as David also speaks of the happiness[^6] of the person to whom God credits righteousness apart from works:
καθάπερ καὶ Δαυὶδ λέγει τὸν μακαρισμὸν τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ᾧ ὁ θεὸς λογίζεται δικαιοσύνην χωρὶς ἔργων·
"Happy are those whose lawless deeds are forgiven, and whose sins are covered.
Μακάριοι ὧν ἀφέθησαν αἱ ἀνομίαι καὶ ὧν ἐπεκαλύφθησαν αἱ ἁμαρτίαι,
Happy is the person whose sin the Lord will never count."[^7]
μακάριος ἀνὴρ οὗ οὐ μὴ λογίσηται κύριος ἁμαρτίαν.
Is this happiness, then, for the circumcised, or also for the uncircumcised? For we say, "Faith was credited to Abraham as righteousness."
Ὁ μακαρισμὸς οὖν οὗτος ἐπὶ τὴν περιτομὴν ἢ καὶ ἐπὶ τὴν ἀκροβυστίαν; λέγομεν γάρ· Ἐλογίσθη τῷ Ἀβραὰμ ἡ πίστις εἰς δικαιοσύνην.
How then was it credited? When he was circumcised, or when he was uncircumcised? Not when he was circumcised, but when he was uncircumcised.
πῶς οὖν ἐλογίσθη; ἐν περιτομῇ ὄντι ἢ ἐν ἀκροβυστίᾳ; οὐκ ἐν περιτομῇ ἀλλʼ ἐν ἀκροβυστίᾳ·

He received the sign of circumcision[^8] as a seal of the righteousness of the faith he had while still uncircumcised. This was so that he would be the father of all who believe without being circumcised, so that righteousness would be credited to them,[^9]
καὶ σημεῖον ἔλαβεν περιτομῆς, σφραγῖδα τῆς δικαιοσύνης τῆς πίστεως τῆς ἐν τῇ ἀκροβυστίᾳ, εἰς τὸ εἶναι αὐτὸν πατέρα πάντων τῶν πιστευόντων διʼ ἀκροβυστίας, εἰς τὸ λογισθῆναι αὐτοῖς τὴν δικαιοσύνην,
and the father of the circumcised who are not only circumcised but who also follow in the footsteps of the faith that our father Abraham had while he was still uncircumcised.[^10]
καὶ πατέρα περιτομῆς τοῖς οὐκ ἐκ περιτομῆς μόνον ἀλλὰ καὶ τοῖς στοιχοῦσιν τοῖς ἴχνεσιν τῆς ἐν ἀκροβυστίᾳ πίστεως τοῦ πατρὸς ἡμῶν Ἀβραάμ.
For the promise to Abraham or to his offspring[^11] that he would inherit the world did not come through the Law but through the righteousness of faith.
Οὐ γὰρ διὰ νόμου ἡ ἐπαγγελία τῷ Ἀβραὰμ ἢ τῷ σπέρματι αὐτοῦ, τὸ κληρονόμον αὐτὸν εἶναι κόσμου, ἀλλὰ διὰ δικαιοσύνης πίστεως·
For if those who rely on the Law[^12] are heirs, faith is made empty and the promise is nullified.
εἰ γὰρ οἱ ἐκ νόμου κληρονόμοι, κεκένωται ἡ πίστις καὶ κατήργηται ἡ ἐπαγγελία·
For the Law brings about wrath, but[^13] where there is no law, there is no transgression either.
ὁ γὰρ νόμος ὀργὴν κατεργάζεται, οὗ δὲ οὐκ ἔστιν νόμος, οὐδὲ παράβασις.

That is why it depends on faith, so that it may rest on grace,[^14] and so that the promise may be guaranteed to all his offspring, not only to those who are of the Law but also to those who are of the faith of Abraham (who is the father of us all,
Διὰ τοῦτο ἐκ πίστεως, ἵνα κατὰ χάριν, εἰς τὸ εἶναι βεβαίαν τὴν ἐπαγγελίαν παντὶ τῷ σπέρματι, οὐ τῷ ἐκ τοῦ νόμου μόνον ἀλλὰ καὶ τῷ ἐκ πίστεως Ἀβραάμ (ὅς ἐστιν πατὴρ πάντων ἡμῶν,
as it is written, "I have made you the father of many nations"),[^15] in the presence of the God in whom he believed, who gives life to the dead and calls into being things that do not exist.[^16]
καθὼς γέγραπται ὅτι Πατέρα πολλῶν ἐθνῶν τέθεικά σε), κατέναντι οὗ ἐπίστευσεν θεοῦ τοῦ ζῳοποιοῦντος τοὺς νεκροὺς καὶ καλοῦντος τὰ μὴ ὄντα ὡς ὄντα·
Hoping against hope, he believed that he would become the father of many nations, according to what had been said: "So will your offspring be."[^17]
ὃς παρʼ ἐλπίδα ἐπʼ ἐλπίδι ἐπίστευσεν εἰς τὸ γενέσθαι αὐτὸν πατέρα πολλῶν ἐθνῶν κατὰ τὸ εἰρημένον· Οὕτως ἔσται τὸ σπέρμα σου·
Without weakening in faith, he considered[^18] his own body, which was as good as dead[^19] (for he was about a hundred years old), and the deadness of Sarah's womb.
καὶ μὴ ἀσθενήσας τῇ πίστει κατενόησεν τὸ ἑαυτοῦ σῶμα νενεκρωμένον, ἑκατονταετής που ὑπάρχων, καὶ τὴν νέκρωσιν τῆς μήτρας Σάρρας,
He did not waver in unbelief concerning the promise of God, but he grew strong in faith, giving glory to God,
εἰς δὲ τὴν ἐπαγγελίαν τοῦ θεοῦ οὐ διεκρίθη τῇ ἀπιστίᾳ ἀλλὰ ἐνεδυναμώθη τῇ πίστει, δοὺς δόξαν τῷ θεῷ
and was fully convinced that God was able to do what he had promised.
καὶ πληροφορηθεὶς ὅτι ὃ ἐπήγγελται δυνατός ἐστιν καὶ ποιῆσαι.
That is why[^20] it was credited to him as righteousness.
διὸ ἐλογίσθη αὐτῷ εἰς δικαιοσύνην.
But the words "it was credited to him" were not written for his sake alone,
Οὐκ ἐγράφη δὲ διʼ αὐτὸν μόνον ὅτι ἐλογίσθη αὐτῷ,
but for ours also. It will be credited to us who believe in him who raised Jesus our Lord from the dead,
ἀλλὰ καὶ διʼ ἡμᾶς οἷς μέλλει λογίζεσθαι, τοῖς πιστεύουσιν ἐπὶ τὸν ἐγείραντα Ἰησοῦν τὸν κύριον ἡμῶν ἐκ νεκρῶν,
who was handed over for our trespasses and raised so that we would be declared righteous.[^21]
ὃς παρεδόθη διὰ τὰ παραπτώματα ἡμῶν καὶ ἠγέρθη διὰ τὴν δικαίωσιν ἡμῶν.

v: Therefore, since we have been declared righteous[^1] by faith, we have peace[^2] with God through our Lord Jesus Christ.
Δικαιωθέντες οὖν ἐκ πίστεως εἰρήνην ἔχομεν πρὸς τὸν θεὸν διὰ τοῦ κυρίου ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ,
Through him we have also obtained access by faith into this grace in which we stand, and we boast[^3] in the hope of the glory of God.
διʼ οὗ καὶ τὴν προσαγωγὴν ἐσχήκαμεν τῇ πίστει εἰς τὴν χάριν ταύτην ἐν ᾗ ἑστήκαμεν, καὶ καυχώμεθα ἐπʼ ἐλπίδι τῆς δόξης τοῦ θεοῦ·
And not only that, but we also boast in our sufferings, knowing that suffering produces endurance,
οὐ μόνον δέ, ἀλλὰ καὶ καυχώμεθα ἐν ταῖς θλίψεσιν, εἰδότες ὅτι ἡ θλῖψις ὑπομονὴν κατεργάζεται,
and endurance produces proven character, and proven character produces hope.
ἡ δὲ ὑπομονὴ δοκιμήν, ἡ δὲ δοκιμὴ ἐλπίδα.
And hope does not put us to shame, because the love of God[^4] has been poured out in our hearts through the Holy Spirit who has been given to us.
ἡ δὲ ἐλπὶς οὐ καταισχύνει· ὅτι ἡ ἀγάπη τοῦ θεοῦ ἐκκέχυται ἐν ταῖς καρδίαις ἡμῶν διὰ πνεύματος ἁγίου τοῦ δοθέντος ἡμῖν.
For while we were still weak, at the right time Christ died for the ungodly.[^5]
Ἔτι γὰρ Χριστὸς ὄντων ἡμῶν ἀσθενῶν ἔτι κατὰ καιρὸν ὑπὲρ ἀσεβῶν ἀπέθανεν.
For one will scarcely die for a righteous person, though for a good person someone might perhaps even dare to die.
μόλις γὰρ ὑπὲρ δικαίου τις ἀποθανεῖται· ὑπὲρ γὰρ τοῦ ἀγαθοῦ τάχα τις καὶ τολμᾷ ἀποθανεῖν·
But God shows his own love for us in this: while we were still sinners, Christ died for us.
συνίστησιν δὲ τὴν ἑαυτοῦ ἀγάπην εἰς ἡμᾶς ὁ θεὸς ὅτι ἔτι ἁμαρτωλῶν ὄντων ἡμῶν Χριστὸς ὑπὲρ ἡμῶν ἀπέθανεν.
Much more, then, since we have now been declared righteous by his blood, will we be saved through him from wrath.
πολλῷ οὖν μᾶλλον δικαιωθέντες νῦν ἐν τῷ αἵματι αὐτοῦ σωθησόμεθα διʼ αὐτοῦ ἀπὸ τῆς ὀργῆς.
For if, while we were enemies, we were reconciled to God through the death of his Son, much more, now that we have been reconciled, will we be saved by his life.
εἰ γὰρ ἐχθροὶ ὄντες κατηλλάγημεν τῷ θεῷ διὰ τοῦ θανάτου τοῦ υἱοῦ αὐτοῦ, πολλῷ μᾶλλον καταλλαγέντες σωθησόμεθα ἐν τῇ ζωῇ αὐτοῦ·
And not only that, but we also boast in God through our Lord Jesus Christ, through whom we have now received reconciliation.
οὐ μόνον δέ, ἀλλὰ καὶ καυχώμενοι ἐν τῷ θεῷ διὰ τοῦ κυρίου ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ, διʼ οὗ νῦν τὴν καταλλαγὴν ἐλάβομεν.
Therefore, just as sin came into the world through one man, and death through sin, and so death spread to all people, because all sinned[^6] —
Διὰ τοῦτο ὥσπερ διʼ ἑνὸς ἀνθρώπου ἡ ἁμαρτία εἰς τὸν κόσμον εἰσῆλθεν καὶ διὰ τῆς ἁμαρτίας ὁ θάνατος, καὶ οὕτως εἰς πάντας ἀνθρώπους ὁ θάνατος διῆλθεν ἐφʼ ᾧ πάντες ἥμαρτον—
for sin was in the world before the Law,[^7] but sin is not counted when there is no law.
ἄχρι γὰρ νόμου ἁμαρτία ἦν ἐν κόσμῳ, ἁμαρτία δὲ οὐκ ἐλλογεῖται μὴ ὄντος νόμου,
Yet death reigned from Adam to Moses, even over those whose sinning was not like the transgression of Adam,[^8] who is a pattern[^9] of the one who was to come.
ἀλλὰ ἐβασίλευσεν ὁ θάνατος ἀπὸ Ἀδὰμ μέχρι Μωϋσέως καὶ ἐπὶ τοὺς μὴ ἁμαρτήσαντας ἐπὶ τῷ ὁμοιώματι τῆς παραβάσεως Ἀδάμ, ὅς ἐστιν τύπος τοῦ μέλλοντος.

But the gift is not like the trespass. For if the many died through the trespass of the one, much more have the grace of God and the gift given by the grace of the one man, Jesus Christ, overflowed to the many.

Ἀλλʼ οὐχ ὡς τὸ παράπτωμα, οὕτως καὶ τὸ χάρισμα· εἰ γὰρ τῷ τοῦ ἑνὸς παραπτώματι οἱ πολλοὶ ἀπέθανον, πολλῷ μᾶλλον ἡ χάρις τοῦ θεοῦ καὶ ἡ δωρεὰ ἐν χάριτι τῇ τοῦ ἑνὸς ἀνθρώπου Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ εἰς τοὺς πολλοὺς ἐπερίσσευσεν.

And the gift is not like what came through the one who sinned. For the judgment following one trespass[^10] led to condemnation, but the gift following many trespasses led to being declared righteous.[^11]
καὶ οὐχ ὡς διʼ ἑνὸς ἁμαρτήσαντος τὸ δώρημα· τὸ μὲν γὰρ κρίμα ἐξ ἑνὸς εἰς κατάκριμα, τὸ δὲ χάρισμα ἐκ πολλῶν παραπτωμάτων εἰς δικαίωμα.

For if, by the trespass of the one, death reigned through that one, much more will those who receive the abundance of grace and of the gift of righteousness reign in life through the one, Jesus Christ.

εἰ γὰρ τῷ τοῦ ἑνὸς παραπτώματι ὁ θάνατος ἐβασίλευσεν διὰ τοῦ ἑνός, πολλῷ μᾶλλον οἱ τὴν περισσείαν τῆς χάριτος καὶ τῆς δωρεᾶς τῆς δικαιοσύνης λαμβάνοντες ἐν ζωῇ βασιλεύσουσιν διὰ τοῦ ἑνὸς Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ.
So then, just as through one trespass condemnation came to all people, so also through one righteous act[^12] there comes to all people the declaration of righteousness that gives life.[^13]
Ἄρα οὖν ὡς διʼ ἑνὸς παραπτώματος εἰς πάντας ἀνθρώπους εἰς κατάκριμα, οὕτως καὶ διʼ ἑνὸς δικαιώματος εἰς πάντας ἀνθρώπους εἰς δικαίωσιν ζωῆς·
For just as through the disobedience of the one man the many were made[^14] sinners, so also through the obedience of the one the many will be made righteous.
ὥσπερ γὰρ διὰ τῆς παρακοῆς τοῦ ἑνὸς ἀνθρώπου ἁμαρτωλοὶ κατεστάθησαν οἱ πολλοί, οὕτως καὶ διὰ τῆς ὑπακοῆς τοῦ ἑνὸς δίκαιοι κατασταθήσονται οἱ πολλοί.
The Law came in alongside, so that the trespass would increase.[^15] But where sin increased, grace overflowed all the more,
νόμος δὲ παρεισῆλθεν ἵνα πλεονάσῃ τὸ παράπτωμα· οὗ δὲ ἐπλεόνασεν ἡ ἁμαρτία, ὑπερεπερίσσευσεν ἡ χάρις,
so that, just as sin reigned in death, so also grace would reign through righteousness to eternal life through Jesus Christ our Lord.
ἵνα ὥσπερ ἐβασίλευσεν ἡ ἁμαρτία ἐν τῷ θανάτῳ, οὕτως καὶ ἡ χάρις βασιλεύσῃ διὰ δικαιοσύνης εἰς ζωὴν αἰώνιον διὰ Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ τοῦ κυρίου ἡμῶν.

n.3: Or "rejoice", "exult"; also in verses 3 and 11. Greek *kauchaomai*, the verb translated "boast" in 2:17, 23.
n.4: That is, God's love for us. Or "our love for God".
n.5: Some manuscripts read "If indeed Christ, while we were still weak, at the right time died for the ungodly".

n.12: Or "through the righteous act of one". Likewise *one trespass* may be "the trespass of one".

v: What then shall we say? Shall we continue in sin so that grace may increase?
Τί οὖν ἐροῦμεν; ἐπιμένωμεν τῇ ἁμαρτίᾳ, ἵνα ἡ χάρις πλεονάσῃ;
By no means! How can we who died to sin still live in it?
μὴ γένοιτο· οἵτινες ἀπεθάνομεν τῇ ἁμαρτίᾳ, πῶς ἔτι ζήσομεν ἐν αὐτῇ;
Or do you not know that all of us who were baptized into Christ Jesus were baptized into his death?
ἢ ἀγνοεῖτε ὅτι ὅσοι ἐβαπτίσθημεν εἰς Χριστὸν Ἰησοῦν εἰς τὸν θάνατον αὐτοῦ ἐβαπτίσθημεν;
So we were buried with him through baptism into death, so that, just as Christ was raised from the dead through the glory of the Father, we too might live a new life.[^1]
συνετάφημεν οὖν αὐτῷ διὰ τοῦ βαπτίσματος εἰς τὸν θάνατον, ἵνα ὥσπερ ἠγέρθη Χριστὸς ἐκ νεκρῶν διὰ τῆς δόξης τοῦ πατρός, οὕτως καὶ ἡμεῖς ἐν καινότητι ζωῆς περιπατήσωμεν.
For if we have been united with him in the likeness of his death,[^2] we will certainly also be united with him in the likeness of his resurrection.
Εἰ γὰρ σύμφυτοι γεγόναμεν τῷ ὁμοιώματι τοῦ θανάτου αὐτοῦ, ἀλλὰ καὶ τῆς ἀναστάσεως ἐσόμεθα·
We know that our old self[^3] was crucified with him, so that the body ruled by sin[^4] might be done away with, so that we would no longer be slaves[^5] to sin.
τοῦτο γινώσκοντες ὅτι ὁ παλαιὸς ἡμῶν ἄνθρωπος συνεσταυρώθη, ἵνα καταργηθῇ τὸ σῶμα τῆς ἁμαρτίας, τοῦ μηκέτι δουλεύειν ἡμᾶς τῇ ἁμαρτίᾳ,
For the one who has died has been set free[^6] from sin.
ὁ γὰρ ἀποθανὼν δεδικαίωται ἀπὸ τῆς ἁμαρτίας.
Now if we died with Christ, we believe that we will also live with him,
εἰ δὲ ἀπεθάνομεν σὺν Χριστῷ, πιστεύομεν ὅτι καὶ συζήσομεν αὐτῷ·
knowing that Christ, having been raised from the dead, will not die again; death no longer has mastery over him.
εἰδότες ὅτι Χριστὸς ἐγερθεὶς ἐκ νεκρῶν οὐκέτι ἀποθνῄσκει, θάνατος αὐτοῦ οὐκέτι κυριεύει·
For the death he died, he died to sin once for all; but the life he lives, he lives to God.
ὃ γὰρ ἀπέθανεν, τῇ ἁμαρτίᾳ ἀπέθανεν ἐφάπαξ· ὃ δὲ ζῇ, ζῇ τῷ θεῷ.
So you also must count yourselves dead to sin but alive to God in Christ Jesus.[^7]
οὕτως καὶ ὑμεῖς λογίζεσθε ἑαυτοὺς εἶναι νεκροὺς μὲν τῇ ἁμαρτίᾳ ζῶντας δὲ τῷ θεῷ ἐν Χριστῷ Ἰησοῦ.
Therefore do not let sin reign in your mortal body, so that you obey its desires.[^8]
Μὴ οὖν βασιλευέτω ἡ ἁμαρτία ἐν τῷ θνητῷ ὑμῶν σώματι εἰς τὸ ὑπακούειν ταῖς ἐπιθυμίαις αὐτοῦ,

Do not offer the parts of your body[^9] to sin as instruments[^10] of unrighteousness, but offer yourselves to God as people brought from death to life, and the parts of your body to God as instruments of righteousness.
μηδὲ παριστάνετε τὰ μέλη ὑμῶν ὅπλα ἀδικίας τῇ ἁμαρτίᾳ, ἀλλὰ παραστήσατε ἑαυτοὺς τῷ θεῷ ὡσεὶ ἐκ νεκρῶν ζῶντας καὶ τὰ μέλη ὑμῶν ὅπλα δικαιοσύνης τῷ θεῷ.
For sin will not be master over you, because you are not under the Law but under grace.
ἁμαρτία γὰρ ὑμῶν οὐ κυριεύσει, οὐ γάρ ἐστε ὑπὸ νόμον ἀλλὰ ὑπὸ χάριν.
What then? Shall we sin because we are not under the Law but under grace? By no means!
Τί οὖν; ἁμαρτήσωμεν ὅτι οὐκ ἐσμὲν ὑπὸ νόμον ἀλλὰ ὑπὸ χάριν; μὴ γένοιτο·
Do you not know that if you offer yourselves to someone as slaves to obey him, you are slaves of the one you obey, either of sin, which leads to death, or of obedience, which leads to righteousness?
οὐκ οἴδατε ὅτι ᾧ παριστάνετε ἑαυτοὺς δούλους εἰς ὑπακοήν, δοῦλοί ἐστε ᾧ ὑπακούετε, ἤτοι ἁμαρτίας εἰς θάνατον ἢ ὑπακοῆς εἰς δικαιοσύνην;
But thanks be to God that you, who were slaves of sin, have obeyed from the heart the pattern of teaching to which you were handed over,[^11]
χάρις δὲ τῷ θεῷ ὅτι ἦτε δοῦλοι τῆς ἁμαρτίας ὑπηκούσατε δὲ ἐκ καρδίας εἰς ὃν παρεδόθητε τύπον διδαχῆς,
and, having been set free from sin, you have become slaves of righteousness.
ἐλευθερωθέντες δὲ ἀπὸ τῆς ἁμαρτίας ἐδουλώθητε τῇ δικαιοσύνῃ·

I am speaking in human terms because of your human weakness.[^12] For just as you once offered the parts of your body as slaves to impurity and to lawlessness, leading to more lawlessness, so now offer them as slaves to righteousness, leading to holiness.[^13]

ἀνθρώπινον λέγω διὰ τὴν ἀσθένειαν τῆς σαρκὸς ὑμῶν· ὥσπερ γὰρ παρεστήσατε τὰ μέλη ὑμῶν δοῦλα τῇ ἀκαθαρσίᾳ καὶ τῇ ἀνομίᾳ εἰς τὴν ἀνομίαν, οὕτως νῦν παραστήσατε τὰ μέλη ὑμῶν δοῦλα τῇ δικαιοσύνῃ εἰς ἁγιασμόν.
For when you were slaves of sin, you were free with regard to righteousness.
Ὅτε γὰρ δοῦλοι ἦτε τῆς ἁμαρτίας, ἐλεύθεροι ἦτε τῇ δικαιοσύνῃ.
So what fruit did you have then from the things of which you are now ashamed?[^14] For the end of those things is death.
τίνα οὖν καρπὸν εἴχετε τότε ἐφʼ οἷς νῦν ἐπαισχύνεσθε; τὸ γὰρ τέλος ἐκείνων θάνατος·
But now that you have been set free from sin and have become slaves of God, the fruit you have leads to holiness, and its end is eternal life.
νυνὶ δέ, ἐλευθερωθέντες ἀπὸ τῆς ἁμαρτίας δουλωθέντες δὲ τῷ θεῷ, ἔχετε τὸν καρπὸν ὑμῶν εἰς ἁγιασμόν, τὸ δὲ τέλος ζωὴν αἰώνιον.
For the wages of sin is death, but the free gift of God is eternal life in Christ Jesus our Lord.
τὰ γὰρ ὀψώνια τῆς ἁμαρτίας θάνατος, τὸ δὲ χάρισμα τοῦ θεοῦ ζωὴ αἰώνιος ἐν Χριστῷ Ἰησοῦ τῷ κυρίῳ ἡμῶν.

v: Or do you not know, brothers and sisters[^1] (for I am speaking to people who know the law),[^2] that the law has authority over a person only as long as that person lives?
Ἢ ἀγνοεῖτε, ἀδελφοί, γινώσκουσιν γὰρ νόμον λαλῶ, ὅτι ὁ νόμος κυριεύει τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ἐφʼ ὅσον χρόνον ζῇ;
For a married woman is bound by law to her husband while he lives; but if her husband dies, she is released from the law concerning her husband.
ἡ γὰρ ὕπανδρος γυνὴ τῷ ζῶντι ἀνδρὶ δέδεται νόμῳ· ἐὰν δὲ ἀποθάνῃ ὁ ἀνήρ, κατήργηται ἀπὸ τοῦ νόμου τοῦ ἀνδρός.

So then, if she marries another man while her husband is alive, she will be called an adulteress. But if her husband dies, she is free from that law, so that she is not an adulteress if she marries another man.
ἄρα οὖν ζῶντος τοῦ ἀνδρὸς μοιχαλὶς χρηματίσει ἐὰν γένηται ἀνδρὶ ἑτέρῳ· ἐὰν δὲ ἀποθάνῃ ὁ ἀνήρ, ἐλευθέρα ἐστὶν ἀπὸ τοῦ νόμου, τοῦ μὴ εἶναι αὐτὴν μοιχαλίδα γενομένην ἀνδρὶ ἑτέρῳ.
So, my brothers and sisters, you also died to the Law through the body of Christ, so that you might belong to another, to him who was raised from the dead, in order that we might bear fruit for God.
Ὥστε, ἀδελφοί μου, καὶ ὑμεῖς ἐθανατώθητε τῷ νόμῳ διὰ τοῦ σώματος τοῦ Χριστοῦ, εἰς τὸ γενέσθαι ὑμᾶς ἑτέρῳ, τῷ ἐκ νεκρῶν ἐγερθέντι ἵνα καρποφορήσωμεν τῷ θεῷ.
For when we were in the flesh,[^3] the sinful passions that came through the Law[^4] were at work in the parts of our body[^5] to bear fruit for death.
ὅτε γὰρ ἦμεν ἐν τῇ σαρκί, τὰ παθήματα τῶν ἁμαρτιῶν τὰ διὰ τοῦ νόμου ἐνηργεῖτο ἐν τοῖς μέλεσιν ἡμῶν εἰς τὸ καρποφορῆσαι τῷ θανάτῳ·
But now we have been released from the Law, having died to what held us captive, so that we serve in the new way of the Spirit and not in the old way of the written code.[^6]
νυνὶ δὲ κατηργήθημεν ἀπὸ τοῦ νόμου, ἀποθανόντες ἐν ᾧ κατειχόμεθα, ὥστε δουλεύειν ἡμᾶς ἐν καινότητι πνεύματος καὶ οὐ παλαιότητι γράμματος.

What then shall we say? Is the Law sin? By no means! Yet I[^7] would not have known sin except through the Law. For I would not have known what it is to covet if the Law had not said, "You must not covet."[^8]
Τί οὖν ἐροῦμεν; ὁ νόμος ἁμαρτία; μὴ γένοιτο· ἀλλὰ τὴν ἁμαρτίαν οὐκ ἔγνων εἰ μὴ διὰ νόμου, τήν τε γὰρ ἐπιθυμίαν οὐκ ᾔδειν εἰ μὴ ὁ νόμος ἔλεγεν· Οὐκ ἐπιθυμήσεις·
But sin, seizing the opportunity through the commandment, produced in me every kind of coveting. For apart from the Law, sin is dead.
ἀφορμὴν δὲ λαβοῦσα ἡ ἁμαρτία διὰ τῆς ἐντολῆς κατειργάσατο ἐν ἐμοὶ πᾶσαν ἐπιθυμίαν, χωρὶς γὰρ νόμου ἁμαρτία νεκρά.
I was once alive apart from the Law, but when the commandment came, sin sprang to life,
ἐγὼ δὲ ἔζων χωρὶς νόμου ποτέ· ἐλθούσης δὲ τῆς ἐντολῆς ἡ ἁμαρτία ἀνέζησεν,
and I died. The very commandment that was meant to bring life proved to bring death to me.
ἐγὼ δὲ ἀπέθανον, καὶ εὑρέθη μοι ἡ ἐντολὴ ἡ εἰς ζωὴν αὕτη εἰς θάνατον·
For sin, seizing the opportunity through the commandment, deceived me,[^9] and through it killed me.
ἡ γὰρ ἁμαρτία ἀφορμὴν λαβοῦσα διὰ τῆς ἐντολῆς ἐξηπάτησέν με καὶ διʼ αὐτῆς ἀπέκτεινεν.
So the Law is holy, and the commandment is holy and righteous and good.
ὥστε ὁ μὲν νόμος ἅγιος, καὶ ἡ ἐντολὴ ἁγία καὶ δικαία καὶ ἀγαθή.

Did what is good, then, become death to me? By no means! Rather, it was sin, so that it might be shown to be sin, producing death in me through what is good, so that through the commandment sin might become utterly sinful.
Τὸ οὖν ἀγαθὸν ἐμοὶ ἐγένετο θάνατος; μὴ γένοιτο· ἀλλὰ ἡ ἁμαρτία, ἵνα φανῇ ἁμαρτία διὰ τοῦ ἀγαθοῦ μοι κατεργαζομένη θάνατον· ἵνα γένηται καθʼ ὑπερβολὴν ἁμαρτωλὸς ἡ ἁμαρτία διὰ τῆς ἐντολῆς.
For we know that the Law is spiritual, but I am made of flesh,[^10] sold as a slave to sin.[^11]
Οἴδαμεν γὰρ ὅτι ὁ νόμος πνευματικός ἐστιν· ἐγὼ δὲ σάρκινός εἰμι, πεπραμένος ὑπὸ τὴν ἁμαρτίαν.
For I do not understand what I do. For I do not do what I want, but I do what I hate.
ὃ γὰρ κατεργάζομαι οὐ γινώσκω· οὐ γὰρ ὃ θέλω τοῦτο πράσσω, ἀλλʼ ὃ μισῶ τοῦτο ποιῶ.
But if I do what I do not want, I agree with the Law that it is good.
εἰ δὲ ὃ οὐ θέλω τοῦτο ποιῶ, σύμφημι τῷ νόμῳ ὅτι καλός.
As it is, it is no longer I who do it, but sin that lives in me.
νυνὶ δὲ οὐκέτι ἐγὼ κατεργάζομαι αὐτὸ ἀλλὰ ἡ οἰκοῦσα ἐν ἐμοὶ ἁμαρτία.
For I know that nothing good lives in me, that is, in my flesh. For the desire to do what is good is present with me, but not the doing of it.[^12]
οἶδα γὰρ ὅτι οὐκ οἰκεῖ ἐν ἐμοί, τοῦτʼ ἔστιν ἐν τῇ σαρκί μου, ἀγαθόν· τὸ γὰρ θέλειν παράκειταί μοι, τὸ δὲ κατεργάζεσθαι τὸ καλὸν οὔ·
For I do not do the good I want, but the evil I do not want is what I do.
οὐ γὰρ ὃ θέλω ποιῶ ἀγαθόν, ἀλλὰ ὃ οὐ θέλω κακὸν τοῦτο πράσσω.
But if I do what I do not want, it is no longer I who do it, but sin that lives in me.
εἰ δὲ ὃ οὐ θέλω τοῦτο ποιῶ, οὐκέτι ἐγὼ κατεργάζομαι αὐτὸ ἀλλὰ ἡ οἰκοῦσα ἐν ἐμοὶ ἁμαρτία.
So I find this law:[^13] when I want to do what is good, evil is present with me.
Εὑρίσκω ἄρα τὸν νόμον τῷ θέλοντι ἐμοὶ ποιεῖν τὸ καλὸν ὅτι ἐμοὶ τὸ κακὸν παράκειται·
For in my inner being[^14] I delight in the law of God,
συνήδομαι γὰρ τῷ νόμῳ τοῦ θεοῦ κατὰ τὸν ἔσω ἄνθρωπον,
but I see another law in the parts of my body, waging war against the law of my mind and taking me captive to the law of sin that is in the parts of my body.
βλέπω δὲ ἕτερον νόμον ἐν τοῖς μέλεσίν μου ἀντιστρατευόμενον τῷ νόμῳ τοῦ νοός μου καὶ αἰχμαλωτίζοντά με ἐν τῷ νόμῳ τῆς ἁμαρτίας τῷ ὄντι ἐν τοῖς μέλεσίν μου.
Wretched man that I am! Who will rescue me from this body of death?[^15]
ταλαίπωρος ἐγὼ ἄνθρωπος· τίς με ῥύσεται ἐκ τοῦ σώματος τοῦ θανάτου τούτου;
Thanks be to God through Jesus Christ our Lord![^16] So then, I myself with my mind serve the law of God, but with my flesh the law of sin.
χάρις τῷ θεῷ διὰ Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ τοῦ κυρίου ἡμῶν. Ἄρα οὖν αὐτὸς ἐγὼ τῷ μὲν νοῒ δουλεύω νόμῳ θεοῦ, τῇ δὲ σαρκὶ νόμῳ ἁμαρτίας.

v: So there is now no condemnation for those who are in Christ Jesus.[^1]
Οὐδὲν ἄρα νῦν κατάκριμα τοῖς ἐν Χριστῷ Ἰησοῦ·
For the law[^2] of the Spirit of life in Christ Jesus has set you[^3] free from the law of sin and of death.
ὁ γὰρ νόμος τοῦ πνεύματος τῆς ζωῆς ἐν Χριστῷ Ἰησοῦ ἠλευθέρωσέν σε ἀπὸ τοῦ νόμου τῆς ἁμαρτίας καὶ τοῦ θανάτου.

For what the Law could not do, because it was weak through the flesh,[^4] God did.[^5] Sending his own Son in the likeness of sinful flesh[^6] and as a sin offering,[^7] he condemned sin in the flesh,
τὸ γὰρ ἀδύνατον τοῦ νόμου, ἐν ᾧ ἠσθένει διὰ τῆς σαρκός, ὁ θεὸς τὸν ἑαυτοῦ υἱὸν πέμψας ἐν ὁμοιώματι σαρκὸς ἁμαρτίας καὶ περὶ ἁμαρτίας κατέκρινε τὴν ἁμαρτίαν ἐν τῇ σαρκί,
so that the righteous requirement of the Law might be fulfilled in us, who live[^8] not according to the flesh but according to the Spirit.
ἵνα τὸ δικαίωμα τοῦ νόμου πληρωθῇ ἐν ἡμῖν τοῖς μὴ κατὰ σάρκα περιπατοῦσιν ἀλλὰ κατὰ πνεῦμα·
For those who belong to the flesh[^9] set their minds on the things of the flesh, but those who belong to the Spirit set their minds on the things of the Spirit.
οἱ γὰρ κατὰ σάρκα ὄντες τὰ τῆς σαρκὸς φρονοῦσιν, οἱ δὲ κατὰ πνεῦμα τὰ τοῦ πνεύματος.
For the mindset of the flesh is death, but the mindset of the Spirit is life and peace,
τὸ γὰρ φρόνημα τῆς σαρκὸς θάνατος, τὸ δὲ φρόνημα τοῦ πνεύματος ζωὴ καὶ εἰρήνη·
because the mindset of the flesh is hostile to God, for it does not submit to the law of God; indeed it cannot.
διότι τὸ φρόνημα τῆς σαρκὸς ἔχθρα εἰς θεόν, τῷ γὰρ νόμῳ τοῦ θεοῦ οὐχ ὑποτάσσεται, οὐδὲ γὰρ δύναται·
Those who are in the flesh cannot please God.
οἱ δὲ ἐν σαρκὶ ὄντες θεῷ ἀρέσαι οὐ δύνανται.
You, however, are not in the flesh but in the Spirit, if indeed the Spirit of God lives in you. But anyone who does not have the Spirit of Christ does not belong to him.
Ὑμεῖς δὲ οὐκ ἐστὲ ἐν σαρκὶ ἀλλὰ ἐν πνεύματι, εἴπερ πνεῦμα θεοῦ οἰκεῖ ἐν ὑμῖν. εἰ δέ τις πνεῦμα Χριστοῦ οὐκ ἔχει, οὗτος οὐκ ἔστιν αὐτοῦ.
But if Christ is in you, the body is dead because of sin, but the Spirit is life because of righteousness.[^10]
εἰ δὲ Χριστὸς ἐν ὑμῖν, τὸ μὲν σῶμα νεκρὸν διὰ ἁμαρτίαν, τὸ δὲ πνεῦμα ζωὴ διὰ δικαιοσύνην.
And if the Spirit of him who raised Jesus from the dead lives in you, he who raised Christ Jesus from the dead will also give life to your mortal bodies because of his Spirit who lives in you.[^11]
εἰ δὲ τὸ πνεῦμα τοῦ ἐγείραντος τὸν Ἰησοῦν ἐκ νεκρῶν οἰκεῖ ἐν ὑμῖν, ὁ ἐγείρας ἐκ νεκρῶν Χριστὸν Ἰησοῦν ζῳοποιήσει καὶ τὰ θνητὰ σώματα ὑμῶν διὰ τὸ ἐνοικοῦν αὐτοῦ πνεῦμα ἐν ὑμῖν.
So then, brothers and sisters,[^12] we are under obligation, not to the flesh, to live according to the flesh.
Ἄρα οὖν, ἀδελφοί, ὀφειλέται ἐσμέν, οὐ τῇ σαρκὶ τοῦ κατὰ σάρκα ζῆν,
For if you live according to the flesh, you will die; but if by the Spirit you put to death the deeds of the body, you will live.
εἰ γὰρ κατὰ σάρκα ζῆτε μέλλετε ἀποθνῄσκειν, εἰ δὲ πνεύματι τὰς πράξεις τοῦ σώματος θανατοῦτε, ζήσεσθε.
For all who are led by the Spirit of God are sons of God.[^13]
ὅσοι γὰρ πνεύματι θεοῦ ἄγονται, οὗτοι υἱοί εἰσιν θεοῦ.
For you did not receive a spirit of slavery that leads you back into fear, but you received the Spirit of adoption,[^14] by whom we cry, "Abba,[^15] Father!"
οὐ γὰρ ἐλάβετε πνεῦμα δουλείας πάλιν εἰς φόβον, ἀλλὰ ἐλάβετε πνεῦμα υἱοθεσίας ἐν ᾧ κράζομεν· Αββα ὁ πατήρ·
The Spirit himself testifies with our spirit that we are children of God.
αὐτὸ τὸ πνεῦμα συμμαρτυρεῖ τῷ πνεύματι ἡμῶν ὅτι ἐσμὲν τέκνα θεοῦ.
And if children, then heirs: heirs of God and fellow heirs with Christ, if indeed we suffer with him so that we may also be glorified with him.
εἰ δὲ τέκνα, καὶ κληρονόμοι· κληρονόμοι μὲν θεοῦ, συγκληρονόμοι δὲ Χριστοῦ, εἴπερ συμπάσχομεν ἵνα καὶ συνδοξασθῶμεν.
For I consider that the sufferings of this present time are not worth comparing with the glory that is going to be revealed to us.
Λογίζομαι γὰρ ὅτι οὐκ ἄξια τὰ παθήματα τοῦ νῦν καιροῦ πρὸς τὴν μέλλουσαν δόξαν ἀποκαλυφθῆναι εἰς ἡμᾶς.
For the creation waits with eager longing for the revealing of the sons of God.
ἡ γὰρ ἀποκαραδοκία τῆς κτίσεως τὴν ἀποκάλυψιν τῶν υἱῶν τοῦ θεοῦ ἀπεκδέχεται·
For the creation was subjected to futility, not willingly, but because of the one who subjected it, in hope
τῇ γὰρ ματαιότητι ἡ κτίσις ὑπετάγη, οὐχ ἑκοῦσα ἀλλὰ διὰ τὸν ὑποτάξαντα, ἐφʼ ἑλπίδι
that[^16] the creation itself will also be set free from its slavery to decay into the freedom of the glory of the children of God.
ὅτι καὶ αὐτὴ ἡ κτίσις ἐλευθερωθήσεται ἀπὸ τῆς δουλείας τῆς φθορᾶς εἰς τὴν ἐλευθερίαν τῆς δόξης τῶν τέκνων τοῦ θεοῦ.
For we know that the whole creation has been groaning together and suffering the pains of childbirth together until now.
οἴδαμεν γὰρ ὅτι πᾶσα ἡ κτίσις συστενάζει καὶ συνωδίνει ἄχρι τοῦ νῦν·
And not only that, but we ourselves, who have the firstfruits of the Spirit, also groan inwardly as we wait eagerly for adoption, the redemption of our bodies.
οὐ μόνον δέ, ἀλλὰ καὶ αὐτοὶ τὴν ἀπαρχὴν τοῦ πνεύματος ἔχοντες ἡμεῖς καὶ αὐτοὶ ἐν ἑαυτοῖς στενάζομεν, υἱοθεσίαν ἀπεκδεχόμενοι τὴν ἀπολύτρωσιν τοῦ σώματος ἡμῶν.
For in this hope we were saved. But hope that is seen is not hope. For who hopes for what he sees?[^17]
τῇ γὰρ ἐλπίδι ἐσώθημεν· ἐλπὶς δὲ βλεπομένη οὐκ ἔστιν ἐλπίς, ὃ γὰρ βλέπει τίς ἐλπίζει;
But if we hope for what we do not see, we wait for it with patience.
εἰ δὲ ὃ οὐ βλέπομεν ἐλπίζομεν, διʼ ὑπομονῆς ἀπεκδεχόμεθα.
In the same way the Spirit also helps us in our weakness. For we do not know what we should pray for as we ought, but the Spirit himself intercedes[^18] with wordless groans.
Ὡσαύτως δὲ καὶ τὸ πνεῦμα συναντιλαμβάνεται τῇ ἀσθενείᾳ ἡμῶν· τὸ γὰρ τί προσευξώμεθα καθὸ δεῖ οὐκ οἴδαμεν, ἀλλὰ αὐτὸ τὸ πνεῦμα ὑπερεντυγχάνει στεναγμοῖς ἀλαλήτοις,
And he who searches hearts knows what the mind of the Spirit is, because he intercedes for God's holy people[^19] according to the will of God.[^20]
ὁ δὲ ἐραυνῶν τὰς καρδίας οἶδεν τί τὸ φρόνημα τοῦ πνεύματος, ὅτι κατὰ θεὸν ἐντυγχάνει ὑπὲρ ἁγίων.
And we know that for those who love God all things work together for good,[^21] for those who are called according to his purpose.
Οἴδαμεν δὲ ὅτι τοῖς ἀγαπῶσι τὸν θεὸν πάντα συνεργεῖ εἰς ἀγαθόν, τοῖς κατὰ πρόθεσιν κλητοῖς οὖσιν.
For those whom he foreknew he also predestined[^22] to be conformed to the image of his Son, so that he would be the firstborn among many brothers and sisters.
ὅτι οὓς προέγνω, καὶ προώρισεν συμμόρφους τῆς εἰκόνος τοῦ υἱοῦ αὐτοῦ, εἰς τὸ εἶναι αὐτὸν πρωτότοκον ἐν πολλοῖς ἀδελφοῖς·
And those whom he predestined he also called; and those whom he called he also declared righteous;[^23] and those whom he declared righteous he also glorified.
οὓς δὲ προώρισεν, τούτους καὶ ἐκάλεσεν· καὶ οὓς ἐκάλεσεν, τούτους καὶ ἐδικαίωσεν· οὓς δὲ ἐδικαίωσεν, τούτους καὶ ἐδόξασεν.
What then shall we say in response to these things? If God is for us, who can be against us?
Τί οὖν ἐροῦμεν πρὸς ταῦτα; εἰ ὁ θεὸς ὑπὲρ ἡμῶν, τίς καθʼ ἡμῶν;
He who did not spare his own Son but handed him over for us all,[^24] how will he not also, with him, graciously give us all things?
ὅς γε τοῦ ἰδίου υἱοῦ οὐκ ἐφείσατο, ἀλλὰ ὑπὲρ ἡμῶν πάντων παρέδωκεν αὐτόν, πῶς οὐχὶ καὶ σὺν αὐτῷ τὰ πάντα ἡμῖν χαρίσεται;
Who will bring a charge against God's chosen ones? It is God who declares righteous.[^25]
τίς ἐγκαλέσει κατὰ ἐκλεκτῶν θεοῦ; θεὸς ὁ δικαιῶν·
Who is to condemn? Christ[^26] is the one who died—more than that, who was raised—who is also at the right hand of God,[^27] who also intercedes for us.
τίς ὁ κατακρινῶν; Χριστὸς ὁ ἀποθανών, μᾶλλον δὲ ἐγερθείς, ὅς καί ἐστιν ἐν δεξιᾷ τοῦ θεοῦ, ὃς καὶ ἐντυγχάνει ὑπὲρ ἡμῶν·
Who will separate us from the love of Christ? Will trouble, or distress, or persecution, or famine, or nakedness, or danger, or sword?
τίς ἡμᾶς χωρίσει ἀπὸ τῆς ἀγάπης τοῦ Χριστοῦ; θλῖψις ἢ στενοχωρία ἢ διωγμὸς ἢ λιμὸς ἢ γυμνότης ἢ κίνδυνος ἢ μάχαιρα;
As it is written: "For your sake we are being killed all day long; we are counted as sheep for the slaughter."[^28]
καθὼς γέγραπται ὅτι Ἕνεκεν σοῦ θανατούμεθα ὅλην τὴν ἡμέραν, ἐλογίσθημεν ὡς πρόβατα σφαγῆς.
No, in all these things we are more than conquerors through him who loved us.
ἀλλʼ ἐν τούτοις πᾶσιν ὑπερνικῶμεν διὰ τοῦ ἀγαπήσαντος ἡμᾶς.
For I am convinced that neither death nor life, neither angels nor rulers,[^29] neither things present nor things to come, nor powers,
πέπεισμαι γὰρ ὅτι οὔτε θάνατος οὔτε ζωὴ οὔτε ἄγγελοι οὔτε ἀρχαὶ οὔτε ἐνεστῶτα οὔτε μέλλοντα οὔτε δυνάμεις
neither height nor depth, nor anything else in all creation will be able to separate us from the love of God that is in Christ Jesus our Lord.
οὔτε ὕψωμα οὔτε βάθος οὔτε τις κτίσις ἑτέρα δυνήσεται ἡμᾶς χωρίσαι ἀπὸ τῆς ἀγάπης τοῦ θεοῦ τῆς ἐν Χριστῷ Ἰησοῦ τῷ κυρίῳ ἡμῶν.

n.2: Or "principle" (see 7:21); also later in the verse.
n.3: *You* is singular in Greek. Many manuscripts read "me".
n.4: Greek *sarx*, "flesh". In Paul's moral sense, human nature in its weakness and opposition to God; so through verse 13.
n.5: The Greek has no verb for this first clause. Literally "For the inability of the Law, in that it was weak through the flesh, God, sending …".
n.7: Or "and for sin". Greek *peri hamartias*, the phrase the Septuagint uses for the sin offering (for example Leviticus 5:6–7; Isaiah 53:10).
n.9: Literally "those who are according to the flesh"; also "according to the Spirit" later in the verse.
n.10: Or "your spirit is alive because of righteousness".
n.11: Some manuscripts read "through his Spirit who lives in you".
n.12: Greek *adelphoi*, "brothers", used of the believers, men and women alike; also in verse 29.
n.13: Greek *huioi*, "sons", as in verse 19. Paul includes all believers, men and women, as heirs (verse 17); in verses 16–17 and 21 he uses *tekna*, "children".
n.14: Or "a spirit of adoption". Greek *huiothesia*, "adoption as sons", the legal act that made someone a son and heir; also in verse 23.
n.17: Many manuscripts read "For why does anyone still hope for what he sees?"
n.21: Or "God works all things together for good", or "in all things God works for good". Some manuscripts read "God works all things together for good".
n.22: Or "decided beforehand". Greek *proorizo*; also in verse 30.
n.25: Compare Isaiah 50:8–9. Verses 33–34 may also be read as questions: "Is it God, who declares righteous? … Is it Christ, who died …?"
n.26: Some manuscripts read "Christ Jesus", and some add "from the dead" after "raised".

v: I am telling the truth in Christ, I am not lying; my conscience bears me witness in the Holy Spirit
Ἀλήθειαν λέγω ἐν Χριστῷ, οὐ ψεύδομαι, συμμαρτυρούσης μοι τῆς συνειδήσεώς μου ἐν πνεύματι ἁγίῳ,
that I have great sorrow and unceasing anguish in my heart.
ὅτι λύπη μοί ἐστιν μεγάλη καὶ ἀδιάλειπτος ὀδύνη τῇ καρδίᾳ μου·
For I could wish that I myself were accursed[^1] and cut off from Christ for the sake of my brothers and sisters,[^2] my own people according to the flesh.[^3]
ηὐχόμην γὰρ ἀνάθεμα εἶναι αὐτὸς ἐγὼ ἀπὸ τοῦ Χριστοῦ ὑπὲρ τῶν ἀδελφῶν μου τῶν συγγενῶν μου κατὰ σάρκα,
They are Israelites. To them belong the adoption,[^4] the glory, the covenants, the giving of the Law, the worship and the promises.
οἵτινές εἰσιν Ἰσραηλῖται, ὧν ἡ υἱοθεσία καὶ ἡ δόξα καὶ αἱ διαθῆκαι καὶ ἡ νομοθεσία καὶ ἡ λατρεία καὶ αἱ ἐπαγγελίαι,
To them belong the patriarchs, and from them, according to the flesh, comes the Messiah,[^5] who is over all, God blessed forever. Amen.[^6]
ὧν οἱ πατέρες, καὶ ἐξ ὧν ὁ χριστὸς τὸ κατὰ σάρκα, ὁ ὢν ἐπὶ πάντων, θεὸς εὐλογητὸς εἰς τοὺς αἰῶνας· ἀμήν.
But it is not as though the word of God has failed. For not all who are descended from Israel are Israel,
Οὐχ οἷον δὲ ὅτι ἐκπέπτωκεν ὁ λόγος τοῦ θεοῦ. οὐ γὰρ πάντες οἱ ἐξ Ἰσραήλ, οὗτοι Ἰσραήλ·
and not all are children because they are Abraham's offspring,[^7] but "It is through Isaac that your offspring will be named."[^8]
οὐδʼ ὅτι εἰσὶν σπέρμα Ἀβραάμ, πάντες τέκνα, ἀλλʼ· Ἐν Ἰσαὰκ κληθήσεταί σοι σπέρμα.
That is, it is not the children of the flesh[^9] who are children of God, but the children of the promise are counted as offspring.
τοῦτʼ ἔστιν, οὐ τὰ τέκνα τῆς σαρκὸς ταῦτα τέκνα τοῦ θεοῦ, ἀλλὰ τὰ τέκνα τῆς ἐπαγγελίας λογίζεται εἰς σπέρμα·
For this is what the promise said: "At this time I will come, and Sarah will have a son."[^10]
ἐπαγγελίας γὰρ ὁ λόγος οὗτος· Κατὰ τὸν καιρὸν τοῦτον ἐλεύσομαι καὶ ἔσται τῇ Σάρρᾳ υἱός.
And not only that, but Rebekah too, when she had conceived children by one man, our father Isaac —
οὐ μόνον δέ, ἀλλὰ καὶ Ῥεβέκκα ἐξ ἑνὸς κοίτην ἔχουσα, Ἰσαὰκ τοῦ πατρὸς ἡμῶν·
for though they were not yet born and had done nothing either good or bad, so that God's purpose in choosing might stand,
μήπω γὰρ γεννηθέντων μηδὲ πραξάντων τι ἀγαθὸν ἢ φαῦλον, ἵνα ἡ κατʼ ἐκλογὴν πρόθεσις τοῦ θεοῦ μένῃ,
not because of works but because of him who calls, she was told, "The older will serve the younger."[^11]
οὐκ ἐξ ἔργων ἀλλʼ ἐκ τοῦ καλοῦντος, ἐρρέθη αὐτῇ ὅτι Ὁ μείζων δουλεύσει τῷ ἐλάσσονι·
As it is written: "Jacob I loved, but Esau I hated."[^12]
καθὼς γέγραπται· Τὸν Ἰακὼβ ἠγάπησα, τὸν δὲ Ἠσαῦ ἐμίσησα.
What then shall we say? Is there injustice[^13] with God? By no means!
Τί οὖν ἐροῦμεν; μὴ ἀδικία παρὰ τῷ θεῷ; μὴ γένοιτο·
For he says to Moses, "I will have mercy on whom I have mercy, and I will have compassion on whom I have compassion."[^14]
τῷ Μωϋσεῖ γὰρ λέγει· Ἐλεήσω ὃν ἂν ἐλεῶ, καὶ οἰκτιρήσω ὃν ἂν οἰκτίρω.
So then it depends not on human will or effort, but on God, who has mercy.[^15]
ἄρα οὖν οὐ τοῦ θέλοντος οὐδὲ τοῦ τρέχοντος ἀλλὰ τοῦ ἐλεῶντος θεοῦ.
For the scripture says to Pharaoh, "For this very purpose I raised you up, to show my power in you, and so that my name may be proclaimed in all the earth."[^16]
λέγει γὰρ ἡ γραφὴ τῷ Φαραὼ ὅτι Εἰς αὐτὸ τοῦτο ἐξήγειρά σε ὅπως ἐνδείξωμαι ἐν σοὶ τὴν δύναμίν μου, καὶ ὅπως διαγγελῇ τὸ ὄνομά μου ἐν πάσῃ τῇ γῇ.
So then he has mercy on whom he wants, and he hardens whom he wants.
ἄρα οὖν ὃν θέλει ἐλεεῖ, ὃν δὲ θέλει σκληρύνει.
You will say to me then, "Why does he still find fault? For who can resist his will?"
Ἐρεῖς μοι οὖν· Τί οὖν ἔτι μέμφεται; τῷ γὰρ βουλήματι αὐτοῦ τίς ἀνθέστηκεν;
On the contrary, who are you, a mere human being,[^17] to talk back to God? Will what is formed say to the one who formed it, "Why did you make me like this?"[^18]
ὦ ἄνθρωπε, μενοῦνγε σὺ τίς εἶ ὁ ἀνταποκρινόμενος τῷ θεῷ; μὴ ἐρεῖ τὸ πλάσμα τῷ πλάσαντι Τί με ἐποίησας οὕτως;
Or does the potter not have the right over the clay, to make from the same lump one vessel for an honorable use and another for a dishonorable use?[^19]
ἢ οὐκ ἔχει ἐξουσίαν ὁ κεραμεὺς τοῦ πηλοῦ ἐκ τοῦ αὐτοῦ φυράματος ποιῆσαι ὃ μὲν εἰς τιμὴν σκεῦος ὃ δὲ εἰς ἀτιμίαν;
What if God, wanting[^20] to show his wrath and to make his power known, has endured with much patience vessels of wrath prepared for destruction,
εἰ δὲ θέλων ὁ θεὸς ἐνδείξασθαι τὴν ὀργὴν καὶ γνωρίσαι τὸ δυνατὸν αὐτοῦ ἤνεγκεν ἐν πολλῇ μακροθυμίᾳ σκεύη ὀργῆς κατηρτισμένα εἰς ἀπώλειαν,
in order to make known the riches of his glory to vessels of mercy, which he prepared beforehand for glory,
καὶ ἵνα γνωρίσῃ τὸν πλοῦτον τῆς δόξης αὐτοῦ ἐπὶ σκεύη ἐλέους, ἃ προητοίμασεν εἰς δόξαν,
even us, whom he also called, not only from the Jews but also from the Gentiles?
οὓς καὶ ἐκάλεσεν ἡμᾶς οὐ μόνον ἐξ Ἰουδαίων ἀλλὰ καὶ ἐξ ἐθνῶν;—
As he also says in Hosea: "Those who were not my people I will call 'my people,' and her who was not loved I will call 'loved.'[^21]
ὡς καὶ ἐν τῷ Ὡσηὲ λέγει· Καλέσω τὸν οὐ λαόν μου λαόν μου καὶ τὴν οὐκ ἠγαπημένην ἠγαπημένην·
And in the place where it was said to them, 'You are not my people,' there they will be called children[^22] of the living God."[^23]
καὶ ἔσται ἐν τῷ τόπῳ οὗ ἐρρέθη αὐτοῖς· Οὐ λαός μου ὑμεῖς, ἐκεῖ κληθήσονται υἱοὶ θεοῦ ζῶντος.
And Isaiah cries out concerning Israel: "Though the number of the Israelites be like the sand of the sea, the remnant will be saved;
Ἠσαΐας δὲ κράζει ὑπὲρ τοῦ Ἰσραήλ· Ἐὰν ᾖ ὁ ἀριθμὸς τῶν υἱῶν Ἰσραὴλ ὡς ἡ ἄμμος τῆς θαλάσσης, τὸ ὑπόλειμμα σωθήσεται·
for the Lord will carry out his word on the earth, completing it and cutting it short."[^24]
λόγον γὰρ συντελῶν καὶ συντέμνων ποιήσει κύριος ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς.
And as Isaiah said beforehand: "If the Lord of Armies[^25] had not left us offspring, we would have been like Sodom; we would have resembled Gomorrah."[^26]
καὶ καθὼς προείρηκεν Ἠσαΐας· Εἰ μὴ κύριος Σαβαὼθ ἐγκατέλιπεν ἡμῖν σπέρμα, ὡς Σόδομα ἂν ἐγενήθημεν καὶ ὡς Γόμορρα ἂν ὡμοιώθημεν.
What then shall we say? That Gentiles, who did not pursue righteousness, have obtained righteousness, the righteousness that comes from faith;
Τί οὖν ἐροῦμεν; ὅτι ἔθνη τὰ μὴ διώκοντα δικαιοσύνην κατέλαβεν δικαιοσύνην, δικαιοσύνην δὲ τὴν ἐκ πίστεως·
but Israel, who pursued a law of righteousness, did not attain to that law.[^27]
Ἰσραὴλ δὲ διώκων νόμον δικαιοσύνης εἰς νόμον οὐκ ἔφθασεν.
Why? Because they did not pursue it by faith, but as if it were by works.[^28] They stumbled over the stone that makes people stumble,
διὰ τί; ὅτι οὐκ ἐκ πίστεως ἀλλʼ ὡς ἐξ ἔργων· προσέκοψαν τῷ λίθῳ τοῦ προσκόμματος,
as it is written: "Look, I am laying in Zion a stone that makes people stumble and a rock that makes them fall, and whoever believes in him[^29] will not be put to shame."[^30]
καθὼς γέγραπται· Ἰδοὺ τίθημι ἐν Σιὼν λίθον προσκόμματος καὶ πέτραν σκανδάλου, καὶ ὁ πιστεύων ἐπʼ αὐτῷ οὐ καταισχυνθήσεται.

n.1: Greek *anathema*, something devoted to God for destruction, and so under a curse.
n.3: That is, by physical descent; also in verses 5 and 8.
n.6: The Greek manuscripts have little punctuation, and the meaning depends on where a full stop is placed. The SBLGNT punctuates as translated here. Others read "the Messiah. God, who is over all, be blessed forever! Amen", or "the Messiah, who is over all. God be blessed forever! Amen".
n.8: Genesis 21:12. Literally "In Isaac seed will be called for you". The verb is *kaleo*, "call", as in verses 12 and 24–26.
n.9: Literally "the children of the flesh", that is, those born by physical descent.
n.14: Exodus 33:19, as in the Septuagint. The Hebrew has "I will be gracious to whom I will be gracious, and I will show compassion to whom I will show compassion".
n.15: Literally "not of the one who wills nor of the one who runs, but of God who has mercy".
n.16: Exodus 9:16. The Hebrew has "I have let you live" (literally "I have caused you to stand"), and "to show you my power".
n.19: Literally "one vessel for honor and another for dishonor". Compare Isaiah 45:9; Jeremiah 18:6.
n.20: Or "although he wanted", or "because he wanted".
n.21: Hosea 2:25 (2:23 in most English Bibles), quoted freely. The Hebrew has "I will have compassion on Lo-ruhamah ('not shown compassion'), and I will say to Lo-ammi ('not my people'), 'You are my people'".
n.22: Greek *huioi*, "sons". The Hebrew of Hosea has *bene*, "sons, children".
n.23: Hosea 2:1 (1:10 in most English Bibles), as in the Septuagint, which has "they will be called" where the Hebrew has "it will be said to them".
n.24: Isaiah 10:22–23, mostly as in the Septuagint; the first line also echoes Hosea 2:1 (1:10 in most English Bibles). The Hebrew reads "only a remnant of them will return. Destruction has been decreed, overflowing with righteousness. For the Lord Yahweh of Armies will carry out the destruction he has decreed in the middle of all the earth". In the Hebrew, "the Lord" is God's personal name, Yahweh. *Completing it and cutting it short*: or "fully and swiftly"; literally "finishing and cutting short a word". Many manuscripts read "for he will finish the word and cut it short in righteousness, because the Lord will carry out a word cut short on the earth", as in the Septuagint.
n.25: Greek *kyrios sabaoth*, from the Hebrew *YHWH tseva'ot*, "Yahweh of Armies", traditionally "the LORD of hosts". In the Hebrew, "the Lord" is God's personal name, Yahweh.
n.26: Isaiah 1:9, as in the Septuagint, which has "offspring" (literally "seed") where the Hebrew has "a few survivors".
n.27: Literally "pursuing a law of righteousness, did not arrive at law". Many manuscripts read "did not attain to the law of righteousness".
n.28: Many manuscripts read "by works of the Law. For they stumbled".
n.29: Or "in it". Many manuscripts read "everyone who believes in him".
n.30: Isaiah 28:16 combined with 8:14. Paul follows the Septuagint of 28:16 in "will not be put to shame", where the Hebrew has "will not panic".

v: Brothers and sisters,[^1] my heart's desire and my prayer to God for them[^2] is for their salvation.
Ἀδελφοί, ἡ μὲν εὐδοκία τῆς ἐμῆς καρδίας καὶ ἡ δέησις πρὸς τὸν θεὸν ὑπὲρ αὐτῶν εἰς σωτηρίαν.
For I testify about them that they have a zeal for God, but it is not based on knowledge.
μαρτυρῶ γὰρ αὐτοῖς ὅτι ζῆλον θεοῦ ἔχουσιν· ἀλλʼ οὐ κατʼ ἐπίγνωσιν,
For, not knowing the righteousness of God, and seeking to establish their own, they did not submit to the righteousness of God.
ἀγνοοῦντες γὰρ τὴν τοῦ θεοῦ δικαιοσύνην, καὶ τὴν ἰδίαν ζητοῦντες στῆσαι, τῇ δικαιοσύνῃ τοῦ θεοῦ οὐχ ὑπετάγησαν·
For Christ is the end of the Law,[^3] so that there may be righteousness for everyone who believes.
τέλος γὰρ νόμου Χριστὸς εἰς δικαιοσύνην παντὶ τῷ πιστεύοντι.
For Moses writes that the person who does the righteousness that comes from the Law will live by it.[^4]
Μωϋσῆς γὰρ γράφει ὅτι τὴν δικαιοσύνην τὴν ἐκ τοῦ νόμου ὁ ποιήσας ἄνθρωπος ζήσεται ἐν αὐτῇ.
But the righteousness that comes from faith says this: "Do not say in your heart,[^5] 'Who will go up to heaven?'" (that is, to bring Christ down),
ἡ δὲ ἐκ πίστεως δικαιοσύνη οὕτως λέγει· Μὴ εἴπῃς ἐν τῇ καρδίᾳ σου· Τίς ἀναβήσεται εἰς τὸν οὐρανόν; τοῦτʼ ἔστιν Χριστὸν καταγαγεῖν·
or, "Who will go down into the abyss?" (that is, to bring Christ up from the dead).[^6]
ἤ· Τίς καταβήσεται εἰς τὴν ἄβυσσον; τοῦτʼ ἔστιν Χριστὸν ἐκ νεκρῶν ἀναγαγεῖν.
But what does it say? "The word is near you, in your mouth and in your heart"[^7] (that is, the word of faith that we proclaim).
ἀλλὰ τί λέγει; Ἐγγύς σου τὸ ῥῆμά ἐστιν, ἐν τῷ στόματί σου καὶ ἐν τῇ καρδίᾳ σου, τοῦτʼ ἔστιν τὸ ῥῆμα τῆς πίστεως ὃ κηρύσσομεν.
For if you confess with your mouth that Jesus is Lord,[^8] and believe in your heart that God raised him from the dead, you will be saved.
ὅτι ἐὰν ὁμολογήσῃς ἐν τῷ στόματί σου κύριον Ἰησοῦν, καὶ πιστεύσῃς ἐν τῇ καρδίᾳ σου ὅτι ὁ θεὸς αὐτὸν ἤγειρεν ἐκ νεκρῶν, σωθήσῃ·
For with the heart one believes, leading to righteousness, and with the mouth one confesses, leading to salvation.
καρδίᾳ γὰρ πιστεύεται εἰς δικαιοσύνην, στόματι δὲ ὁμολογεῖται εἰς σωτηρίαν·
For the scripture says, "Everyone who believes in him will not be put to shame."[^9]
λέγει γὰρ ἡ γραφή· Πᾶς ὁ πιστεύων ἐπʼ αὐτῷ οὐ καταισχυνθήσεται.
For there is no distinction between Jew and Greek. The same Lord is Lord of all, and he is rich toward all who call on him.
οὐ γάρ ἐστιν διαστολὴ Ἰουδαίου τε καὶ Ἕλληνος, ὁ γὰρ αὐτὸς κύριος πάντων, πλουτῶν εἰς πάντας τοὺς ἐπικαλουμένους αὐτόν·
For "everyone who calls on the name of the Lord will be saved."[^10]
Πᾶς γὰρ ὃς ἂν ἐπικαλέσηται τὸ ὄνομα κυρίου σωθήσεται.
How then will they call on him in whom they have not believed? And how will they believe in him whom they have not heard?[^11] And how will they hear without someone to preach?
Πῶς οὖν ἐπικαλέσωνται εἰς ὃν οὐκ ἐπίστευσαν; πῶς δὲ πιστεύσωσιν οὗ οὐκ ἤκουσαν; πῶς δὲ ἀκούσωσιν χωρὶς κηρύσσοντος;
And how will they preach unless they are sent? As it is written: "How beautiful are the feet of those who bring good news of good things!"[^12]
πῶς δὲ κηρύξωσιν ἐὰν μὴ ἀποσταλῶσιν; καθὼς γέγραπται· Ὡς ὡραῖοι οἱ πόδες τῶν εὐαγγελιζομένων τὰ ἀγαθά.
But not all have obeyed the good news. For Isaiah says, "Lord, who has believed our message?"[^13]
ἀλλʼ οὐ πάντες ὑπήκουσαν τῷ εὐαγγελίῳ· Ἠσαΐας γὰρ λέγει· Κύριε, τίς ἐπίστευσεν τῇ ἀκοῇ ἡμῶν;
So faith comes from hearing the message, and the message comes through the word of Christ.[^14]
ἄρα ἡ πίστις ἐξ ἀκοῆς, ἡ δὲ ἀκοὴ διὰ ῥήματος Χριστοῦ.
But I ask, have they not heard? Indeed they have: "Their sound has gone out into all the earth, and their words to the ends of the world."[^15]
Ἀλλὰ λέγω, μὴ οὐκ ἤκουσαν; μενοῦνγε· Εἰς πᾶσαν τὴν γῆν ἐξῆλθεν ὁ φθόγγος αὐτῶν, καὶ εἰς τὰ πέρατα τῆς οἰκουμένης τὰ ῥήματα αὐτῶν.
But I ask, did Israel not understand? First Moses says, "I will make you jealous with what is not a nation; with a foolish nation I will provoke you."[^16]
ἀλλὰ λέγω, μὴ Ἰσραὴλ οὐκ ἔγνω; πρῶτος Μωϋσῆς λέγει· Ἐγὼ παραζηλώσω ὑμᾶς ἐπʼ οὐκ ἔθνει, ἐπʼ ἔθνει ἀσυνέτῳ παροργιῶ ὑμᾶς.
And Isaiah is bold enough to say, "I was found by those who did not seek me; I showed myself to those who did not ask for me."[^17]
Ἠσαΐας δὲ ἀποτολμᾷ καὶ λέγει· Εὑρέθην ἐν τοῖς ἐμὲ μὴ ζητοῦσιν, ἐμφανὴς ἐγενόμην τοῖς ἐμὲ μὴ ἐπερωτῶσιν.
But concerning Israel he says, "All day long I have held out my hands to a disobedient and contrary people."[^18]
πρὸς δὲ τὸν Ἰσραὴλ λέγει· Ὅλην τὴν ἡμέραν ἐξεπέτασα τὰς χεῖράς μου πρὸς λαὸν ἀπειθοῦντα καὶ ἀντιλέγοντα.

n.8: Some manuscripts read "if you confess with your mouth the word that Jesus is Lord".
n.9: Isaiah 28:16, as in the Septuagint (see 9:33), with "everyone" added.

n.11: Or "of whom they have not heard".

v: So I ask, has God rejected his people?[^1] By no means! For I myself am an Israelite, a descendant of Abraham,[^2] of the tribe of Benjamin.
Λέγω οὖν, μὴ ἀπώσατο ὁ θεὸς τὸν λαὸν αὐτοῦ; μὴ γένοιτο· καὶ γὰρ ἐγὼ Ἰσραηλίτης εἰμί, ἐκ σπέρματος Ἀβραάμ, φυλῆς Βενιαμίν.
God has not rejected his people, whom he foreknew. Or do you not know what the scripture says in the passage about Elijah,[^3] how he pleads with God against Israel?
οὐκ ἀπώσατο ὁ θεὸς τὸν λαὸν αὐτοῦ ὃν προέγνω. ἢ οὐκ οἴδατε ἐν Ἠλίᾳ τί λέγει ἡ γραφή, ὡς ἐντυγχάνει τῷ θεῷ κατὰ τοῦ Ἰσραήλ;
"Lord, they have killed your prophets, they have torn down your altars; I alone am left, and they are seeking my life."[^4]
Κύριε, τοὺς προφήτας σου ἀπέκτειναν, τὰ θυσιαστήριά σου κατέσκαψαν, κἀγὼ ὑπελείφθην μόνος, καὶ ζητοῦσιν τὴν ψυχήν μου.
But what was God's answer to him? "I have kept for myself seven thousand men who have not bowed the knee to Baal."[^5]
ἀλλὰ τί λέγει αὐτῷ ὁ χρηματισμός; Κατέλιπον ἐμαυτῷ ἑπτακισχιλίους ἄνδρας, οἵτινες οὐκ ἔκαμψαν γόνυ τῇ Βάαλ.
So too at the present time there is a remnant, chosen by grace.
οὕτως οὖν καὶ ἐν τῷ νῦν καιρῷ λεῖμμα κατʼ ἐκλογὴν χάριτος γέγονεν·
And if it is by grace, it is no longer by works; otherwise grace would no longer be grace.[^6]
εἰ δὲ χάριτι, οὐκέτι ἐξ ἔργων, ἐπεὶ ἡ χάρις οὐκέτι γίνεται χάρις.
What then? What Israel is seeking, it has not obtained. The chosen have obtained it, but the rest were hardened,
τί οὖν; ὃ ἐπιζητεῖ Ἰσραήλ, τοῦτο οὐκ ἐπέτυχεν, ἡ δὲ ἐκλογὴ ἐπέτυχεν· οἱ δὲ λοιποὶ ἐπωρώθησαν,
as it is written: "God gave them a spirit of stupor, eyes that would not see and ears that would not hear, to this very day."[^7]
καθὼς γέγραπται· Ἔδωκεν αὐτοῖς ὁ θεὸς πνεῦμα κατανύξεως, ὀφθαλμοὺς τοῦ μὴ βλέπειν καὶ ὦτα τοῦ μὴ ἀκούειν, ἕως τῆς σήμερον ἡμέρας.
And David says: "Let their table become a trap and a net, a snare and a retribution for them.
καὶ Δαυὶδ λέγει· Γενηθήτω ἡ τράπεζα αὐτῶν εἰς παγίδα καὶ εἰς θήραν καὶ εἰς σκάνδαλον καὶ εἰς ἀνταπόδομα αὐτοῖς,
Let their eyes be darkened so that they cannot see, and bend their backs continually."[^8]
σκοτισθήτωσαν οἱ ὀφθαλμοὶ αὐτῶν τοῦ μὴ βλέπειν, καὶ τὸν νῶτον αὐτῶν διὰ παντὸς σύγκαμψον.
So I ask, did they stumble so as to fall? By no means! Rather, through their trespass salvation has come to the Gentiles, to make them jealous.
Λέγω οὖν, μὴ ἔπταισαν ἵνα πέσωσιν; μὴ γένοιτο· ἀλλὰ τῷ αὐτῶν παραπτώματι ἡ σωτηρία τοῖς ἔθνεσιν, εἰς τὸ παραζηλῶσαι αὐτούς.
Now if their trespass means riches for the world, and their failure means riches for the Gentiles, how much more will their full inclusion[^9] mean!
εἰ δὲ τὸ παράπτωμα αὐτῶν πλοῦτος κόσμου καὶ τὸ ἥττημα αὐτῶν πλοῦτος ἐθνῶν, πόσῳ μᾶλλον τὸ πλήρωμα αὐτῶν.
Now I am speaking to you Gentiles.[^10] Inasmuch then as I am an apostle to the Gentiles, I make much of my ministry,
Ὑμῖν δὲ λέγω τοῖς ἔθνεσιν. ἐφʼ ὅσον μὲν οὖν εἰμι ἐγὼ ἐθνῶν ἀπόστολος, τὴν διακονίαν μου δοξάζω,
in the hope that somehow I may make my own people[^11] jealous and save some of them.
εἴ πως παραζηλώσω μου τὴν σάρκα καὶ σώσω τινὰς ἐξ αὐτῶν.
For if their rejection means the reconciliation of the world, what will their acceptance mean but life from the dead?
εἰ γὰρ ἡ ἀποβολὴ αὐτῶν καταλλαγὴ κόσμου, τίς ἡ πρόσλημψις εἰ μὴ ζωὴ ἐκ νεκρῶν;
If the firstfruits are holy, so is the whole batch of dough;[^12] and if the root is holy, so are the branches.
εἰ δὲ ἡ ἀπαρχὴ ἁγία, καὶ τὸ φύραμα· καὶ εἰ ἡ ῥίζα ἁγία, καὶ οἱ κλάδοι.
But if some of the branches were broken off, and you, though a wild olive shoot, were grafted in among them and came to share in the rich root[^13] of the olive tree,
Εἰ δέ τινες τῶν κλάδων ἐξεκλάσθησαν, σὺ δὲ ἀγριέλαιος ὢν ἐνεκεντρίσθης ἐν αὐτοῖς καὶ συγκοινωνὸς τῆς ῥίζης τῆς πιότητος τῆς ἐλαίας ἐγένου,
do not boast over the branches. If you do boast, remember that you do not support the root, but the root supports you.
μὴ κατακαυχῶ τῶν κλάδων· εἰ δὲ κατακαυχᾶσαι, οὐ σὺ τὴν ῥίζαν βαστάζεις ἀλλὰ ἡ ῥίζα σέ.
You will say then, "Branches were broken off so that I could be grafted in."
ἐρεῖς οὖν· Ἐξεκλάσθησαν κλάδοι ἵνα ἐγὼ ἐγκεντρισθῶ.
That is true. They were broken off because of unbelief, but you stand by faith. Do not be arrogant, but be afraid.
καλῶς· τῇ ἀπιστίᾳ ἐξεκλάσθησαν, σὺ δὲ τῇ πίστει ἕστηκας. μὴ ὑψηλὰ φρόνει, ἀλλὰ φοβοῦ·
For if God did not spare the natural branches, neither will he spare you.[^14]
εἰ γὰρ ὁ θεὸς τῶν κατὰ φύσιν κλάδων οὐκ ἐφείσατο, οὐδὲ σοῦ φείσεται.
Note then the kindness and the severity of God: severity toward those who fell, but God's kindness toward you, if you continue in his kindness. Otherwise you too will be cut off.
ἴδε οὖν χρηστότητα καὶ ἀποτομίαν θεοῦ· ἐπὶ μὲν τοὺς πεσόντας ἀποτομία, ἐπὶ δὲ σὲ χρηστότης θεοῦ, ἐὰν ἐπιμένῃς τῇ χρηστότητι, ἐπεὶ καὶ σὺ ἐκκοπήσῃ.
And they too, if they do not continue in unbelief, will be grafted in, for God is able to graft them in again.
κἀκεῖνοι δέ, ἐὰν μὴ ἐπιμένωσι τῇ ἀπιστίᾳ, ἐγκεντρισθήσονται· δυνατὸς γάρ ἐστιν ὁ θεὸς πάλιν ἐγκεντρίσαι αὐτούς.

For if you were cut from what is by nature a wild olive tree and grafted, contrary to nature, into a cultivated olive tree, how much more will these natural branches be grafted into their own olive tree!
εἰ γὰρ σὺ ἐκ τῆς κατὰ φύσιν ἐξεκόπης ἀγριελαίου καὶ παρὰ φύσιν ἐνεκεντρίσθης εἰς καλλιέλαιον, πόσῳ μᾶλλον οὗτοι οἱ κατὰ φύσιν ἐγκεντρισθήσονται τῇ ἰδίᾳ ἐλαίᾳ.

For I do not want you to be unaware of this mystery, brothers and sisters,[^15] so that you may not be wise in your own sight: a hardening has come on part of Israel[^16] until the full number[^17] of the Gentiles has come in,
Οὐ γὰρ θέλω ὑμᾶς ἀγνοεῖν, ἀδελφοί, τὸ μυστήριον τοῦτο, ἵνα μὴ ἦτε ἑαυτοῖς φρόνιμοι, ὅτι πώρωσις ἀπὸ μέρους τῷ Ἰσραὴλ γέγονεν ἄχρι οὗ τὸ πλήρωμα τῶν ἐθνῶν εἰσέλθῃ,
and in this way[^18] all Israel will be saved. As it is written: "The Deliverer will come from Zion; he will turn away ungodliness from Jacob.
καὶ οὕτως πᾶς Ἰσραὴλ σωθήσεται· καθὼς γέγραπται· Ἥξει ἐκ Σιὼν ὁ ῥυόμενος, ἀποστρέψει ἀσεβείας ἀπὸ Ἰακώβ.
And this will be my covenant with them, when I take away their sins."[^19]
καὶ αὕτη αὐτοῖς ἡ παρʼ ἐμοῦ διαθήκη, ὅταν ἀφέλωμαι τὰς ἁμαρτίας αὐτῶν.
As regards the good news, they are enemies for your sake; but as regards election, they are loved for the sake of the patriarchs.
κατὰ μὲν τὸ εὐαγγέλιον ἐχθροὶ διʼ ὑμᾶς, κατὰ δὲ τὴν ἐκλογὴν ἀγαπητοὶ διὰ τοὺς πατέρας·
For the gifts and the calling of God are irrevocable.
ἀμεταμέλητα γὰρ τὰ χαρίσματα καὶ ἡ κλῆσις τοῦ θεοῦ.
For just as you were once disobedient to God but have now received mercy because of their disobedience,
ὥσπερ γὰρ ὑμεῖς ποτε ἠπειθήσατε τῷ θεῷ, νῦν δὲ ἠλεήθητε τῇ τούτων ἀπειθείᾳ,
so they too have now been disobedient, so that by the mercy shown to you they too may now receive mercy.[^20]
οὕτως καὶ οὗτοι νῦν ἠπείθησαν τῷ ὑμετέρῳ ἐλέει ἵνα καὶ αὐτοὶ νῦν ἐλεηθῶσιν·
For God has shut up all in disobedience so that he may have mercy on all.
συνέκλεισεν γὰρ ὁ θεὸς τοὺς πάντας εἰς ἀπείθειαν ἵνα τοὺς πάντας ἐλεήσῃ.
Oh, the depth of the riches and wisdom and knowledge of God![^21] How unsearchable are his judgments, and how untraceable his ways!
Ὦ βάθος πλούτου καὶ σοφίας καὶ γνώσεως θεοῦ· ὡς ἀνεξεραύνητα τὰ κρίματα αὐτοῦ καὶ ἀνεξιχνίαστοι αἱ ὁδοὶ αὐτοῦ.
For who has known the mind of the Lord? Or who has been his counselor?[^22]
Τίς γὰρ ἔγνω νοῦν κυρίου; ἢ τίς σύμβουλος αὐτοῦ ἐγένετο;
Or who has given to him first, so that he should be repaid?[^23]
ἢ τίς προέδωκεν αὐτῷ, καὶ ἀνταποδοθήσεται αὐτῷ;
For from him and through him and to him are all things. To him be the glory forever. Amen.
ὅτι ἐξ αὐτοῦ καὶ διʼ αὐτοῦ καὶ εἰς αὐτὸν τὰ πάντα· αὐτῷ ἡ δόξα εἰς τοὺς αἰῶνας, ἀμήν.
